articles.title: Millwall 2-2 West Ham: Mohamadou Kante scores and then sent off as Hammers fight back to draw at the Den
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Millwall and West Ham United at the Den; Lions led through Caleb Taylor and Camiel Neghli first-half goals but Mohamadou Kante and Konstantinos Mavropanos earn Hammers a point, despite Kante's late red
articles.body:
The half-time sub had helped change the game for the visitors, arrowing into the bottom corner from 25 yards to launch the comeback. The Hammers then levelled on 80 minutes when Konstantinos Mavropanos headed in at the back post and looked set to push on for a winner.

But Kante brought down Kyrell Lisbie with a last-man foul after he had been caught in possession to receive the fourth red card in the past seven meetings between these sides and Lyndon Dykes blasted over a last-gasp chance for the Millwall to clinch it.

It was a dramatic conclusion to a game which lived up to its billing, 14 years on from the last Dockers derby.

The home side overwhelmed West Ham in the first half. Close-range goals from Caleb Taylor and Camiel Neghli from Dykes long throws summed up their physical approach.

It could have been an even better first 45 for Millwall had Mark Sykes' screamer against the bar from 35 yards gone in.

West Ham had been well short of the intensity levels required for this fixture to that point but changed the narrative after the break. Wave after wave of attack on the Millwall goal eventually brought them the rewards to retain local pride and top spot in the Championship - although a first win at Millwall since 1988 proved elusive.

On 65 minutes, the match was stopped when Millwall goalkeeper Filip Marschall made an accusation that West Ham forward Taty Castellanos had spat at him. Play resumed without any action taken.

Afterwards, Millwall boss Alex Neil said: "I haven't asked [Marschall] about it. I'm sure there will be footage of it or not of it if it didn't happen. I'd be extremely surprised if Filip has made an accusation and nothing has happened. The fourth official said there was an accusation of spitting."

West Ham boss Nuno Espirito Santo said: "I'm aware of the allegation. I didn't see the image, I didn't speak with Taty. I cannot go much further on that. I'm going to look at the images but I cannot answer."

16: GOAL! Caleb Taylor forces the opener in after Mads Hemansen saves from Mark Sykes and Tairyk Arconte when Lyndon Dykes' long throw caused chaos in the West Ham box.

45: OFF THE BAR! Sykes cracks the ball against the crossbar from 35 yards out.

45+1: GOAL! Camiel Neghli scores Millwall's second from close range after another Dykes long throw comes to him in the box, capping a brilliant first half for the Lions.

46: SUBS! West Ham make a double change at the break with Mohamadou Kante and Pablo sent on.

52: CHANCE! Jarrod Bowen's shot is parried by Filip Marschall and the goalkeeper just reacts in time to prevent Kante tucking in the loose ball.

67: SAVE! A stunning one-hand stop from Marschall keeps out Pablo's header.

74: GOAL! Kante arrows a low shot into the bottom corner from 25 yards to pull one back for the Hammers.

76: SIDE-NETTING! Jarrod Bowen is teed up in the box by Taty Castellanos but his shot is deflected just the wrong side of the near post as the Hammers mount wave after wave of attacks.

80: GOAL! Konstantinos Mavropanos heads in Manor Solomon's cross from a short corner at the back post to level it up!

89: RED CARD! Kante is sent off after bringing down Kyrell Lisbie when he was clean through on goal.

90+3: OVER! Dykes sends a half-volley flying over the bar from inside the West Ham box.

"Mixed emotions. It was an unbelievable effort from the players. they left everything on the pitch, as you would hope for. We just ran out of steam as the game wore on. There was a lack of freshness in options, particularly at the top end of the pitch. I thought [Lyndon Dykes] and [Tairyk Arconte] were excellent, caused them all sorts of problems in the first half. But once we hit about 60-65 minutes, we really tired.

"So 2-0 up, brilliant first half, probably should have been more. They then changed their shape to a 3-5-2 and we found it really difficult to get out. We lost energy in the middle, we lost energy in the top line and ended up sinking and sinking.

"The frustrating thing from my perspective is the goals come from a 30-yard shot from outside the box and a second-phase set-play. All in all, I couldn't ask any more of the lads."

"Clearly the first half we didn't go well in the game, we didn't start well, we were not precise, we lost balls, we didn't deal with the physicality of Millwall. They are so good and strong, they took advantage of the throw-in, the way we can see things happening.

"Disappointing on that part, we knew what we were going to find but we didn't do well.

"But much improved in the second half and the way the game went, it's a positive. Not what we wanted but the way the boys reacted to a bad first half was good and positive."

On Kante's red card: "He came into the game very well, a beautiful goal but then a big mistake and then it was the right decision to take it and avoid something tragical.

"He's a very young player, a lot of things to improve - we have many in our squad - so I hope this is a lesson for his future."

articles.title: Nottingham Forest vs Coventry City: Why unusually tough start should not be used to measure Frank Lampard's side
articles.summary: Coventry City have endured a miserable return to the Premier League, but all is not lost four games in - Frank Lampard is experienced enough to know that; watch Nottingham Forest vs Coventry City live on Sky Sports Main Event on Saturday; kick-off 5.30pm
articles.body:
Arsenal, Man City and Brighton are among the top-flight's established elite. Brighton are currently the league's top scorers, albeit five came against Coventry last weekend. High-flying Hull City are perhaps the only outlier where achievable points were dropped.

Frank Lampard's side remain pointless and without a goal heading into matchweek five. "We went one down from a moment of quality. Welcome to the Premier League," he said after defeat to Brighton, the step up in class obviously overwhelming for a squad who could only boast five players with any meaningful Premier League experience (measured as 20+ appearances).

But the city of Coventry knows all about adversity. Supporters have felt its brute force many times since slipping out of the Premier League in 2001. Four defeats is not enough to break them. Fans at the CBS Arena on Saturday made a demonstration of defiance; they will not turn their backs having fought so hard just to be here. That helps Lampard's cause immeasurably.

Coventry are competing - but only sporadically. They are aerially dominant but seem to be losing the battle on the ground. Their press is quick and co-ordinated in some areas of the pitch and not others. They create chances but do not score. Adapting to the demands in every department will be key to survival.

The physical profile of their squad should at least ensure they will not be bullied out of this division. Becoming more bullish and imposing themselves, with the conviction that they belong, is the next step. Leeds are a relevant example to draw inspiration from.

Daniel Farke's side pressure and duel their way to victories, with success rooted largely in what they do against the ball. They are hard to beat because of it. Jamie Carragher's summary of Leeds' most recent win over Newcastle on MNF tallies with that: "Newcastle have been beaten up by a really good Premier League team."

As a newly promoted side, Coventry need to get to grips with a compact shape and be aggressive with its implementation. Stylistically, it's why the club targeted giants in the summer transfer window. Winger Loum Tchaouna was the only new recruit to arrive for a significant who stands below 6ft.

If Lampard can establish a collective robustness that meets the physical demands of this league, the absence of individual star quality should matter less. Teams who rarely get outrun or outfought are often among the survivors when May rolls around.

Creatively, the Sky Blues are better than their non-existent goal tally suggests. According to expected goals (xG) data, they should have scored four already. When analysing xGOT, which evaluates the quality of an on-target attempt, that total increases to five.

Unsurprisingly, then, it stands to reason that opposition goalkeepers have played their part in such a miserable start. Gianluigi Donnarumma kept Man City alive at the Etihad, as did Konstantinos Tzolakis in defeat to Hull. Coventry lost both games by a one-goal margin.

Despite being comprehensively beaten by Brighton after Taiwo Awoniyi was sent off, player of the match Bart Verbruggen was forced into six saves. When Lewis Dunk is scoring screamers from 30 yards, his first goal from open play at the grand age of 34, you know luck has landed elsewhere.

Coventry have conceded three goals from outside the box overall, more than any other side. That suggests an issue with pressing distances, allowing opponents too much space in striking zones, but could just as easily be explained by the increase in level and tempo. The Premier League is full of tormentors. Lewis Dunk apparently among them.

But Lampard's experience should prevent any imposter syndrome setting in. The former Chelsea midfielder knows the league intimately, as a coach and a player. He understands how unforgiving it can be and will not be downtrodden by what has already happened - most of it expected.

As he prepares his side for a trip to Nottingham Forest on Saturday, live on Sky Sports , he can point to who they have played and how they have competed in parts. There is something to be said for getting visits to the Emirates and the Etihad out of the way while the scrap for points is far less consequential.

The City Ground, however, is where potential lies. Forest are yet to score a league goal at home this season. In fact, since last Christmas, the only ever-present side with fewer home points than Forest is Spurs. Coventry travel to the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium next month. Both are games with the possibility for points.

Not the moment for a crisis of confidence, then. Lampard will be hoping one win is all it takes to release his players from the harshness of the Premier League. They badly need a boost.

articles.title: Nottingham Forest stadium expansion approved - so what now?
articles.summary: Will the dream of a bigger City Ground finally become a reality?
articles.body:
For Nottingham Forest fans, this has been a long time coming.

The last time the City Ground saw any major redevelopment work, Stuart Pearce and Stan Collymore still played for the Reds.

With the ground regularly reaching capacity since returning to the Premier League, the club's case for expansion seems pretty clear.

But there has been talk of redevelopment for at least seven years now , and besides the addition of a temporary stand made of shipping containers and some cosmetic improvements, the stadium remains much as it was in the mid-90s.

So after all the artist's impressions and a seemingly endless series of council meetings, fans will be forgiven for asking - is it for real this time?

The approval given earlier this week is a huge step towards the plans becoming a reality.

The reason that never went ahead is simple.

After several consecutive seasons in the top flight and a European campaign under its belt, the club now have bigger ambitions.

The new proposals, unveiled a matter of months after the old ones were rubber-stamped, do not quite mean the redevelopment has to start from scratch.

But their sheer scale does mean extra considerations for the authorities and fresh planning permission was necessary.

After all, it will involve up to 21,300 more people flocking to a part of Nottinghamshire that is already incredibly busy on a matchday - a 68% increase.

For transparency, I speak from experience as a lifelong Forest fan myself. But - believe it or not - not everyone is, and councils have to consider the impact on all residents, whether they are fans or not.

In areas close to the ground such as Lady Bay, for example, there are long-running issues with parking.

Ward councillor Richard Mallender said while he was happy to see the stadium expand, he added the volume of traffic regularly led to buses being cancelled and residents being trapped in their homes.

"We're not here to block things, we don't want to stop things," he said.

"What we want to do is make sure this really successful team have the stadium they need, but that it also works for the people who live here," he said.

He, like other councillors, support the introduction of a controlled parking zone (CPZ), which could see parking banned within a 25-minute walk of the ground for four hours either side of kick-off, except for residents and businesses.

Planning law does not require an applicant to solve existing problems unless what they are proposing is likely to exacerbate them, and so Forest are set to contribute £990,000 towards establishing the CPZ.

It is just one part of a £4.1m package aimed at getting more people to the ground without using their cars.

There is scepticism from councillors about how well this strategy - known as "modal shift" - will actually work, but it is set to be monitored by a new transport working group made up of the club, councils, and other stakeholders.

Even if a lot more people arrive by foot, however, there is the small matter of getting many of them over the River Trent.

After highways authorities rejected a proposal to permanently close two traffic lanes on Trent Bridge, managing crowd flow has become the biggest outstanding issue.

Indeed, the planning report states "the pedestrian capacity of Trent Bridge is the principal constraint on the development".

But rather than let it scupper the whole application, it has instead been made a planning condition, which states the club can proceed with the expansion provided it comes up with another solution.

This does not necessarily have to be a new pedestrian and cycle bridge, but councils either side of the river have made it clear that is their preferred option.

It has sparked fears among fans that it would mean Forest have to build a new bridge before redeveloping the stadium, potentially adding yet more years to the process.

Instead, the planning condition is structured, so the club cannot start demolition work until a new crowd flow solution - which may or may not be a bridge - has been agreed upon.

They then would not be allowed any occupancy of the stadium above the current capacity until that solution is delivered.

In other words, the club could build the stadium and the hypothetical bridge at the same time.

There is also a further provision, which allows for temporary measures for up to 18 months if the permanent solution looks set to take longer than the time it takes to rebuild the stadium.

The club has not yet said what it intends to do, but speaking earlier this week the East Midlands mayor Claire Ward seemed to suggest her office could contribute.

"If you look at where we've unlocked other opportunities in different places through investments, that's certainly within the realm of what we do, but clearly we would need to have a business case and we'd need to look at the details," she said.

Chairman of the Nottingham Forest Supporters' Trust, Asif Naidu, said the travel issues were "clearly not insurmountable".

"I think we've been open in saying we want to work with stakeholders, that includes the club, our members, and the wider supporter group to understand what can be done, how can supporters and the trust help try and overcome some of those hurdles," he said.

Crowd flow is clearly the biggest barrier to getting spades in the ground, but it is not the only one.

The plans involve demolishing the Britannia Boathouse, home to the Nottingham Rowing Club.

Forest have agreed to provide like-for-like facilities somewhere else, which the rowing club supports, but planning documents say although some alternative locations have been discussed, nothing has been confirmed yet.

And crucially, the legal agreement that has been drawn up states the current boathouse cannot be demolished until either a replacement is built, or temporary facilities are found followed by a permanent replacement within three years.

Then there is the unresolved matter of who owns the land upon which the stadium sits.

After a public row over rent two years ago, which even prompted talk of relocation from the City Ground, an agreement was eventually reached to buy the freehold from the city council.

That deal was based on the club getting permission to expand the stadium which, of course, it has now been given - twice.

But at the time of writing, I understand the deal is yet to go through and the council still owns the land.

I have heard nothing to suggest it cannot now be finalised, and I am not sure anyone at the council or club would want to reopen those wounds - but it is another point on the TBC list.

With all the above and more still to be sorted out, no date has been set for the redevelopment to begin, so many supporters may still be thinking, they'll believe it when they see it.

A crucial difference between now and what has come before though, is that the latest plans align more closely with club owner Evangelos Marinakis's vision for the City Ground.

Speaking at a press conference ahead of Forest's home game against Coventry, head coach Oliver Glasner said he had discussed the stadium expansion with Marinakis when they met earlier in the week.

"It's great news for the club, it's great news for the city, it's great news for our supporters and I think everybody is now looking forward to when the works will start," Glasner said.

There are a lot of fans who would love to know when exactly that will be.

articles.title: La Fábrica, príncipe mundial
articles.standfirst: El Juvenil A madridista conquista la Copa Intercontinental sub 20, el título que le faltaba a la cantera, al vencer 3-1 al Santiago Wanderers con goles de Yáñez, Santamaría y Roberto Martín en una final marcada por el juego sucio chileno
articles.summary: El Juvenil A madridista conquista la Copa Intercontinental sub 20, el título que le faltaba a la cantera, al vencer 3-1 al Santiago Wanderers con goles de Yáñez, Santamaría y Roberto Martín en una final marcada por el juego sucio chileno
articles.body: Estos 'niños' son muy grandes. Lo llevan demostrando meses, y este sábado lo rubricaron haciendo historia sobre el césped del Bernabéu, donde el Juvenil A del Real Madrid conquistó la Copa Intercontinental sub-20, el último título que le faltaba a La Fábrica para rematar su vitrina, y además en la primera final de esta competición disputada en suelo europeo. No fue un camino de rosas. Fue, más bien, una batalla campal. Tras adelantarse por medio de Yáñez y sufrir el empate chileno, hizo falta un tanto de Santamaría en el tramo final y otro de Roberto Martín en el descuento para dejar en la lona a un áspero Santiago Wanderers (que terminó con tres expulsados) y coronar a los chavales de Álvaro López como campeones del mundo de su categoría. El círculo queda cerrado con el cetro mundial descansando en Valdebebas. La Fábrica se vistió de gala y el Bernabéu respondió a la altura. Ni José Mourinho, presente en un palco, se lo quiso perder. Más de 50.000 espectadores, que le arrebataron a Maracaná el récord de asistencia en un partido juvenil, arroparon a la 'galaxia juvenil' de Álvaro López en su busca del entorchado, con cerca de 3.000 aficionados chilenos poniendo el contrapunto en las gradas. No era para menos, pues en el once inicial figuraban hasta seis futbolistas que ya habían debutado con el primer equipo madridista, tres de ellos incluso en partido oficial. El partido, que arrancó bajo el mando blanco, se enturbió a partir del cuarto de hora por varias acciones antideportivas del correoso Santiago Wanderers. Alexis Ciria respondió a una de ellas y se llevó una amarilla por su arrojo, pero la siguiente ya no admitió indulgencia. El colegiado polaco no tembló y expulsó al chileno Dubó con roja directa por un plantillazo temerario sobre Yáñez. Fue precisamente esa falta la que abrió el camino de la gloria. El propio 7 madridista fue el ejecutor del correctivo desde fuera del área, en el sector diestro, con un golpeo a media altura que se perdió entre una maraña de piernas blancas y verdes. Avello, el meta wanderino, no alcanzó a ver el esférico hasta que este ya se colaba por su costado derecho. Con un futbolista menos y el marcador en contra, Salinas movió ficha de inmediato retirando a Flores para dar entrada a Jaramillo. La tensión, que había amenazado con desbordarse, fue amainando conforme el Madrid, envalentonado por su renta, tomaba las riendas y se liberaba de nervios. La sorpresa iba a llegar tras el paso por vestuarios. Un error de Mario Rivas en salida de balón permitió recuperar a Christian Silva, quien definió en un mano a mano ante Javi Navarro para igualar la contienda. No menguó el conjunto de Álvaro López a pesar del jarro de agua fría. Un cabezazo de Yeremaiah estuvo cerca de adelantar de nuevo a los blancos, que se refrescaron con las piernas de Liberto y Roberto Martín. Y cuando el contador marcaba el minuto 70, fue Javi Navarro quien tuvo que erigirse en salvador para tapar un disparo de Vargas que pudo resultar mortal. Álvaro López agitó entonces el banquillo, y ahí encontró el resquicio hacia la gloria. Una internada de Fortea hasta la línea de fondo por la derecha encontró al recién ingresado Santamaría, que apareció en el área pequeña para embocar el balón. El 2-1, a falta de ocho minutos y el añadido, desató la fiesta en un Bernabéu entregado. El tramo final, que discurrió entre revisiones de VAR, asistencias médicas y expulsiones, se hizo eterno por culpa de las continuas interrupciones de un cuadro chileno más preocupado en exhibir cancherismo que en practicar fútbol. Un tormento. Pero La Fábrica ya tenía el trono a la vista con el tanto del lastimado Roberto Martín minutos después de que Yáñez marrase un penalti en el descuento. Real Madrid: Javi Navarro; Fortea, Joan Martínez, Mario Rivas (Liberto, 61'), Aguado (Lezcano, 46'); Sergio Martínez (Roberto Martín, 61'), Cestero (Santamaría, 80'), Carlos Díez (Lacosta, 75'); Yáñez, Yeremaiah y Ciria. Entrenador: Álvaro López. Santiago Wanderers: Avello; A. Silva (Lagos, 78'), Valenzuela, Adasme, Dubó; Avendaño (Carvacho, 78'), Villarroel, Ponce; Flores (Jaramillo, 32'), C. Silva (San Martín, 65') y V. Vargas (S. Vargas, 78'). Entrenador: Felipe Salinas. Goles: Yáñez 1-0 (29'), C. Silva 1-1 (49'), Santamaría 2-1 (81'), Roberto Martín 3-1 (90+9'). Penalti fallado por Yáñez (90+5'). Árbitro: Damian Sylwestrzak (polaco): Amonestó con amarilla a Ciria (21') A. Silva (21'), Villarroel (31'), Vargas (35'), Valenzuela (85' y 87'), Liberto (86'), S. Vargas (90+3'), San Martín (90+6'), Joan Martínez (90+6'). Amonestó con roja directa a Dubó (25') y Carvacho (90+6'). Estadio: Santiago Bernabéu. 52.117 espectadores (récord mundial de asistencia en un partido de categoría juvenil).

articles.title: Tottenham 0-2 Aston Villa: Tottenham struggles continue after Villa win
articles.summary: Tottenham are still looking for their first Premier League goal of the season.
articles.body:
Aston Villa piled more misery on Tottenham with a comfortable win.

Johan Manzambi, Nicolas Jackson and Emi Buendia struck as Villa earned their first league victory of the season.

Conor Gallagher and Jan Paul van Hecke scored late for Spurs but it was not enough.

Here's how BBC Sport rated the players and you can see how you scored them below.

Antonin Kinsky: Made a comfortable save from Manzambi's strike before a better one thwarted Buendia. There was little he could do to stop the goals. 6

Pedro Porro: Back after missing the draws against Nottingham Forest and Everton but his returned lasted 18 minutes as he limped off injured. Had made a positive start. 6

Jan Paul van Hecke: It looked a robust performance as he handled the nuisance of Jackson when Villa did venture forward but he was beaten by Manzambi to the ball for the opener. Scored late consolation. 6

Micky van de Ven: Took a blow to the face just before the break and was off the pitch for treatment when Villa scored, which summed up Spurs' afternoon. 5

Andrew Robertson: Made a mistake in trying to keep the ball in, which eventually led to Villa's first. Thought he had atoned, only to be ruled offside in the build-up to Kudus' disallowed goal. 5

Sandro Tonali: One first-half strike whistled wide but it was another underwhelming outing for the £100m midfielder. 5

Rodrigo Bentancur: Enjoyed the battle in an occasionally congested midfield but his influenced waned as the game wore on. 5

Savio: The forward should have put Spurs ahead early and an excellent volley was kept out by Suzuki, but after a strong opening 25 minutes he failed to build. 5

Mateus Fernandes: Replaced at half-time as Tottenham chased the game, the former West Ham midfielder the victim of the circumstances . 6

Omar Marmoush: The Manchester City loanee was brought in to get the goals but it was a listless display once the game started to go away from Tottenham . 5

Dominic Solanke: The striker has not scored in the Premier League since March and could not find a telling touch again. There was little to suggest his drought would end. 5

Archie Gray (on 18, Porro): Could have scored with his first touch but was denied by Suzuki. That was as good as it got. 6

Mohammed Kudus (on 46, Fernandes): Came on with Tottenham needing more attacking impetus and had a goal disallowed but was not able to spark. 5

James Maddison (on 66, Solanke): The substitute was unable to make an impact from the bench. 5

Conor Gallagher (on 84, Tonali). Late consolation was his second goal in successive games.

Subs not used: Dubravka, Tosin, Senesi, Udogie.

Villa survive late Spurs fightback to earn first Premier League win

Zion Suzuki: Kept Villa level with saves from Savio and Archie Gray in the first half. A fine performance but his usually excellent distribution let him down. 8

Aaron Wan-Bissaka: The right-back has struggled to adapt quickly under Unai Emery. One slip almost cost Villa a goal and was little surprise he was withdrawn at half-time. 5

Tyrone Mings: Lost the ball several times as Villa played out from the back but rediscovered his composure after the break. 6

Victor Lindelof: Relatively untroubled in the second half after needing to be alert to Spurs' early threat. Once that died down, it was a comfortable afternoon. 7

Matteo Ruggeri: A full Premier League debut for the left-back but he did not look convincing as he tries to understand what is needed by Emery. 6

Joao Gomes: In his first Premier League appearance after his opening-weekend dismissal, the midfielder was solid and able to protect Villa's lead. 7

Boubacar Kamara: It was the midfielder's shot which fell into the path of Manzambi to score, and he was able to keep Villa moving. 7

John McGinn: His tenacity was rewarded as he seized on Roberton's error to help set up Manzambi's goal. A typically dynamic display. 7

Emi Buendia: The forward loves a goal at Tottenham and scored the pick of the bunch when he found the top corner from 25 yards to seal it. 7

Johan Manzambi: A goal and an assist on his full debut for Villa as he grew into the game after a slow start when Tottenham dominated. More will be expected once he settles in. 8

Nicolas Jackson: Isolated for long spells in the first half but got his goal in the second and was a nuisance. Had earlier forced Kinsky into a smartsave. 7

Matty Cash (on 46, Wan-Bissaka): The right-back returned from injury to help strengthen Villa's defence. 7

George Hemmings (on 72, Manzambi): Helped Villa to a comfortable win.

Unused subs: Wright, Bogarde, Abraham, Garnacho, Harwood-Bellis.

articles.title: Emery y su Aston Villa salen a flote... hundiendo en desgracia al Tottenham
articles.standfirst: Los 'villanos' logran su primera victoria en Premier goleando a unos 'spurs' (2-3) que, al menos, celebró sus primeros goles en el campeonato doméstico
articles.summary: Los 'villanos' logran su primera victoria en Premier goleando a unos 'spurs' (2-3) que, al menos, celebró sus primeros goles en el campeonato doméstico
articles.body: Ha tardado cinco jornadas en llegar. Pero, después de la profunda reconstrucción que se han visto obligados a completar en verano, Emery y su Aston Villa ya tienen en el bolsillo la primera victoria en la Premier 26-27 a consta de un Tottenham (2-3) que sigue sin ganar... y se conformó con celebrar sus primeros goles del curso en el campeonato doméstico. De Zerbi, un día más, seguía probando variantes en busca de dar con la tecla que permita despegar a su Tottenham, que venía de caer eliminado ante el Liverpool en Carabao. Can Marmoush tirado a banda, fue Mateus Fernandes quien agarró la mediapunta. Emery, por su parte, le regaló a Manzambi su primera titularidad con el Aston Villa tras disputar sus dos primeros partidos -llegó lesionado- desde el banquillo. La doble intervención de Suzuki ante Sávio levantó a las gradas de un Tottenham Hotspur Stadium que, sin embargo, se quedó helado con la lesión de Pedro Porro. Ausente por unos problemas físicos durante los últimos encuentros, sintió un 'pinchazo' en la parte posterior del muslo y tuvo que abandonar el verde a los 19' en favor de Archie Gray. Su presencia con España, salvo sorpresa, está completamente descartada. No volvió a encontrar continuidad en sus ataques el Tottenham... aunque es cierto que Suzuki se siguió luciendo con alguna que otra intervención de mérito. Salvo una mano a Buendía, tampoco Kinsky tuvo que aparecer en exceso. Pero, mientras Van de Ven pedía entrar al campo tras recibir un 'topetazo' en el ojo, Manzambi embocó un disparo en semifallo' de Kamara que puso por delante a los 'villanos' en el descuento. Reaccionó De Zerbi dando entrada al descanso a un Mohammed Kudus que se ubicó como mediapunta por delante del doble pivote formado por Bentancur y Tonali. Se quedó en el vestuario un Mateus Fernandes que no termina de arrancar en el Tottenham después de protagonizar un traspaso cercano a los 100 millones de euros. El Aston Villa se limitó a juntarse atrás para intentar 'matar' el partido a la contra apoyándose en la autosuficiencia al espacio de Nico Jackson. Se fue diluyendo el Tottenham y, por si fuera poco, Kudus vio anulado el gol del empate justo cuando se cumplía la hora de encuentro por fuera de juego previo de Robertson. Se sucedían las desgracias en el Tottenham y, nada más entrar Maddison al terreno de juego, Nico Jackson hizo el 0-2 en el 68'. Suzuki buscó en largo al senegalés, le ganó el duelo a Van de Ven, combinó con Manzambi y se abrió espacio para definir de volea. Puso la mano blanda Kinsky... que nada pudo hacer para detener el 0-3 de Emi Buendía en el 78' tras conectar un remate directo a la escuadra desde el balcón del área. La cara de circunstancias de Roberto de Zerbi en el banquillo era la de alguien que sabe que, por delante, va a tener que afrontar un parón de selecciones que se le puede hacer extremadamente largo. Desfilaban los aficionados por los aledaños. Gallagher, al menos, se apuntó el primer tanto en Premier de este Tottenham cuando todo estaba decidido... y Van Hecke ajustó el marcador en la última jugada del choque.

articles.summary: El técnico del Juvenil A analizó la victoria en la final de la Copa Intercontinental sub 20
articles.body: Álvaro López está viviendo un año de ensueño. El técnico del Juvenil A del Real Madrid compareció ante los medios tras conquistar la Copa Intercontinental sub 20, el título que le faltaba a La Fábrica, y analizó una victoria por 3-1 ante el Santiago Wanderers que corona un curso irrepetible en su carrera. Conquista del título: "Imagina para un madridista como yo, que soy socio desde pequeño y he vivido mil noches históricas. Es un orgullo increíble, tenemos que dar las gracias al club y a la afición". Partido rudo: "Las finales el Madrid no las juega, las gana. Ha sido muy intenso, nos lo han puesto muy difícil. Lo importante era disfrutar de un escenario como el de hoy (el Bernabéu), es algo histórico y nos lo llevamos para el recuerdo". Presencia de Florentino y Mou: "El presi nos ha dado la enhorabuena. Estamos muy agradecidos del apoyo de ambos. Sentir este apoyo es algo que nos vamos a llevar para siempre". Techo de la generación: "Es una generación histórica, han ganado la Youth y la Copa Intercontinental. Esto es de ellos. Están a un paso de llegar al fútbol profesional, estamos muy orgullosos de ellos y representan a la perfección los valores del Real Madrid". ¿Cómo se siente ser campeón del mundo?: "Es increíble poder hacerlo con compañeros que llevo desde los 8 ó 9 años. Hacerlo aquí en este estadio es algo muy especial".

articles.title: El pistolero Adri Fuentes dispara al Mallorca
articles.standfirst: El equipo bermellón vuelve a ganar con un gol de su delantero, que ya suma cuatro tantos en Liga
articles.summary: El equipo bermellón vuelve a ganar con un gol de su delantero, que ya suma cuatro tantos en Liga
articles.body: El Mallorca se impuso por 0-1 al Sanse en Zubieta, gracias al gol de Adrián Fuentes en la parte final de un partido que, en su primera parte, tuvo al filial como dominador y poseedor de hasta seis ocasiones claras, pero sin materializar alguna por falta de puntería y las paradas de Arnau Tenas. Sanse y Mallorca buscaron la victoria desde el pitido inicial, sobre todo por la misma banda, la derecha de ataque de los locales, con Dani Díaz y con Liso, por unos y otros, como jugadores más incisivos por ese carril, que fue de ida y vuelta. De hecho, tras un disparo centrado de Astiazaran a las manos de Arnau Tenas, el portero balear detuvo un chut cercano de Dani Díaz ajustado a un poste izquierdo que luego rozó un nuevo derechazo de Astiazaran. Carrera, con otra pelota que salió cerca del otro palo, evidenció la superioridad de los de Ansotegi en ocasiones de gol. El equipo de Luis García buscó tener más balón y ralentizar algo el correcalles, y lo consiguió durante bastantes minutos, hasta que el Sanse tuvo cuatro córners seguidos, el tercero por meter Arnau Tenas las dos manos ante un fuerte zurdazo de Dani Díaz, que insistió, con el portero catalán despejando en esta ocasión de puños. Casi antes del descanso, Adri Fuentes, de espuela, tuvo la más clara para el Mallorca, pero el balón se le fue un metro desviado. Tras el paso por los vestuarios hubo un amago de regreso al ida y vuelta, pero las defensas, más agresivas, faltas incluidas, lo evitaron y no hubo oportunidades claras. Luis García, que ya había dado entrada a Arnau Puigmal en el descanso, echó mano de Antoniu Roca y Josep Cerdà para buscar el gol de la victoria, pero los dos, como otro incorporado como John Chetauya, dispararon arriba. Cuando parecía que el 0-0 no se iba a mover, Adri Fuentes terminó una muy buena acción individual superando a Fraga de disparo cruzado y firmó un gol que vale tres puntos muy importantes para el Mallorca.

articles.title: El Rayo, con Camello al galope
articles.standfirst: El madrileño, que lleva 7 goles en 7 jornadas, araña un punto ante Osasuna, que se había adelantado con golazo de Budimir
articles.summary: El madrileño, que lleva 7 goles en 7 jornadas, araña un punto ante Osasuna, que se había adelantado con golazo de Budimir
articles.body: Osasuna y Rayo empatan a todo. A goles, a puntos y a sensaciones. Incluso sus delanteros están con la flecha para arriba, porque fueron Budimir y Camello los que perforaron las áreas y sellaron el reparto de puntos de Pamplona. Empezaron avisando los rayistas con un disparo de De Frutos en los primeros minutos. El atacante, que volvía a a jugar y conectaba un fuerte disparo abajo que despejaba Aitor. El portero, que evitó unos días antes que la goleada del Atlético fuera aún mayor, repetía en detrimento de Sergio Herrera. Pese al dominio inicial de los madrileños, Osasuna fuen quien mojó primero. Una gran acción por banda de Kike Barja, un centro al área, un mal despeja de Álvaro García fueron la antesala al golazo del día en Pamplona. Budimir la controla orientado con el pecho, giro y disparo de volea para reventar la red. Maravillosa acción en una baldosa del croata. El gol contagió la intensidad al cuadro rojillo, que fue entonces el dueño del partido ante un Rayo que parecía algo aturdido. Sin embargo, los de Beñat lograron despejarse y terminar dominando la primera parte. Sin ocasiones claras, pero con síntomas de lo que podíamos ver en la reanudación. Las sensaciones se materializaron a los pocos minutos de la segunda parte. Una gran jugada de Pedrosa por su banda izquierda terminó con un centro para Camello, que no perdonó en la primera que tuvo. Séptimo gol del delantero empatando con Mbappé y Lamine Yamal. Números estratosféricos para un ariete del Rayo en apenas siete jornadas ligueras. Se rehízo, sin embargo, Osasuna. Ramis movió rápido el banquillo para volver a ponerse por delante en el marcador. Numerosos cambios que, no obstante, no dieron el rendimiento esperado y, pese a dominar el juego, las ocasiones brillaban por su ausencia. Viendo el poco peligro en su portería, el cuadro rayista también quiso mover piezas para rascar dos puntos más. En el tramo final le entraron las prisas a ambos conjuntos, siendo el equipo pamplonica el que con más ímpetu buscaba la portería contraria, pero sin éxito. Y, para colmo, lesión de Raúl Moro. El extremo, que se había dejado ver, sigue sin terminar de explotar en la formación rojilla. Al final, ninguno contento ni ninguno descontento. Reparto justo de puntos y a seguir pensando en sumar como sea para encarrilar un mismo objetivo: la salvación.

articles.title: Cardiff City 3-1 Charlton: Jack Moylan double steers Bluebirds to first win of the season
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Cardiff City and Charlton Athletic at the Cardiff City Stadium on Saturday; Jack Moylan double steers Bluebirds to a first victory of the campaign.
articles.body:
The Bluebirds had gone a record-equalling seven games without a win despite dominating a number of their previous matches, but they were full value for their triumph after taking a 2-0 lead in the opening quarter against a Charlton side that came into the fixture sitting in sixth place with only one league defeat.

Moylan scored the first goal in the eighth minute, teed up Yousef Salech for the second in the 24th and then thundered in his second, and Cardiff's third, in the 61st after Tyreece Campbell had reduced the deficit.

Charlton's physicality and pressing meant it took Cardiff some time to settle into their passing rhythm and the first chance of the game fell to Miles Leaburn after good work down the left flank from Karlan Grant and Campbell.

Once they found their composure, the Bluebirds conjured up a a great first goal from Moylan. It started, as with so many of Cardiff's best moves, with Chris Willock on the left edge of box before moving infield to Andy Robertson.

Robertson then passed forward, Moylan stepped over the ball to let it roll on to Salech, who then passed back to the Irishman on the edge of the 'D' to give him a clear shot on goal and he buried the ball in the right-hand corner to give his side a dream start.

Willock had a shot that was heading into the same corner pushed wide by Arthur Okonkwo in the Charlton goal, but Cardiff came again and doubled their lead in the 24th minute.

This time it was Moylan who returned the favour to Salech as he sent an inch-perfect pass across the six-yard box to allow the striker to tap home his fifth goal of the season in all competitions.

Charlton looked stunned, but they were quick to respond and five minutes later Campbell ran on to a superb through ball from Tyler Bindon that cut the Cardiff lines and gave his striker a one-on-one with Nathan Trott in the home goal and he made no mistake.

Okonkwo was called on to pull off a great save from Salech before the break and Joel Colwill should have done better in front of goal when he had a chance to add to Cardiff's tally.

There was still all to play for after the break and things might have been different had Cardiff old boy Grant not hit the side-netting instead of the back of the net after picking up a poor back pass.

Then came Moylan's second just past the hour mark. He worked the ball out of Ollie Tanner on the right edge of the box, took a return pass and fired home an unstoppable shot into the top-right corner to make the game safe.

"It was a very important game for us. We felt as if we'd been playing reasonably well and we have to do it again. We knew today's game was going to be tough, but we played a great game, created really good chances and we took enough of them to win.

"We obviously had a real awareness of what Charlton do and how effective they can be, but we got into the spaces we needed to and created good chances. I was particularly pleased with the response to conceding the goal because that was obviously a test for us.

"We bounced back pretty much straight away and kept creating good chances. In the second half, I felt as if we ran out deserving winners.

"You don't always get what you feel you deserve. We were clear with the players that there were certain games where we weren't at our best, but we had full belief that if we kept playing the way we were playing and managed to score the goals we felt we would, we could win the game.

"We felt as if we were bringing a player who would improve the squad when we bought Jack Moylan. He has qualities we probably didn't have before.

"He's a very dangerous player in the situations you saw him in today. The big appeal for us was because of where he's come from, he has a lot of improvement in him. The way he's working means he will improve a lot and become a great player for the club."

"It's an unrecognisable performance to what we normally do. We got outworked, outbattled, outran, outpassed, outthought - everything about it.

"Ironically, we've had three massive chances in the game, but that would only have papered over the cracks of a really poor performance.

"We give Cardiff credit because they played well, but we allowed them to do what they wanted. Our intensity in our press, reading the second balls, our physicality - all of it meant it was quite easy to play against us, that's the big thing I'm embarrassed about.

"We were inept. How we pressed, the work-rate we had - we were really poor. That's not taking anything from Cardiff, because Cardiff would have had to do something right to have really tested us, but that's an unacceptable performance from us out of possession, and that's why we conceded what we did.

"To get any foothold in the game, you have to pass the ball well enough, and we didn't. When they pressed us, we just gave the ball away, so we were never able to build anything. All in all, that's a really poor performance from us."

articles.title: Stoke 2-1 Sheffield United: Potters hit back for victory at Sam Gallagher nets stunner
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Stoke City and Sheffield United at the bet365 Stadium on Saturday; Jack McGlynn and Sam Gallagher score in comeback victory.
articles.body:
Two goals in the space of 11 breathtaking second-half minutes from Jack McGlynn and super-sub Sam Gallagher saw the Potters turn the game on its head and make it an impressive four wins in their last five Sky Bet Championship fixtures.

Kalvin Phillips' first league goal for five-and-a-half years, a 51st-minute long-range free-kick, had put the Blades on course for what would have been only their second away league win of the season.

But McGlynn levelled for the hosts in the 78th minute with a left-foot screamer - his second goal in as many games - and Gallagher completed a battling fightback with a sublime 86th-minute volley which was worthy of winning any game.

The unchanged home side started the brighter of the two sides and could have been ahead after only 12 minutes.

Djibril Soumare had time and space but rifled his left-foot shot from the edge of the area straight at an alert Michael Cooper.

Lamine Cisse, making his 150th career appearance, fired wide of the target shortly afterwards as the hosts pressed for an opener.

And just before the half-hour mark Ben Johnson cut inside after receiving the ball wide on the right, only to power his left-foot shot at Cooper.

The Blades bounced out of the blocks at the start of the second half and Sydie Peck, recently called up to the England Under-21 squad, blazed a left-foot shot over from a decent position on the edge of the box.

And, not long after, the visitors took the lead thanks to a spot of individual brilliance from Phillips and much to the delight of the 1,939 travelling fans.

The 30-year-old lined up a free-kick from distance and somehow squeezed his shot past Viktor Johansson at his near post. In truth, the experienced Sweden international goalkeeper will know he should have done a lot better.

The goal was just what was needed to ignite the contest and Stoke deservedly equalised through McGlynn's super strike.

Eric Bocat had moments earlier tested Cooper and, with momentum on their side, Gallagher stole the show with his late winner, superbly bringing the ball down before volleying home.

"If those goals don't deserve to win a football match, then I don't know what level of quality does.

"That's testament to Sam Gallagher. For him to have worked to keep coming back from injury and disappointment, well that is just a demonstration of sheer brute force and quality that gets you a winning goal in what was a really tight game.

"The first goal was good enough, that's Jack all over. But Sam's goal, well that's one of the best goals I've ever seen.

"We worked really hard to get back on level terms after conceding what we felt was a real giveaway (goal).

"But the support and energy in the stadium was really good - and it needed to be because after the run of fixtures we've had, it's been tough for everyone.

"There's been so many games in this period, it's been really tough, so the players deserve an awful lot of credit.

"The start we had wasn't brilliant, but they picked up the mantle, got some confidence going and we've shown we've got some genuine quality.

"It's exciting (our form), that's the emotion I feel. I'm a lot happier with where we're at after the start we had."

"It was a tough one to take for us all. Unfortunately fine margins decide games, but I can't fault the players because they put everything out there.

"We got our noses in front but they find two wonder goals which decided the game for them.

"When two players whack in goals from 30 yards then it's nothing to do with our quality.

"It was a tight game, but we could have quite easily been sat here with six points from the last two games, but two wonder goals have decided it.

"To concede two goals like that one in game, well I don't think you'll concede two goals like that again all season.

"We have to deal with the disappointment, but the Championship is difficult, there's no getting around that.

"But it quickly changes and now we've got the international break to get some players back and to improve on things.

"The players are super tight and I'm super tight with them. They're really disappointed we've not got a result, but you've got to get through tough times like this. That's what professional football is all about."

articles.title: El jugador más joven y más veterano en marcar en el derbi madrileño: dos leyendas del Real Madrid tiene este récord
articles.standfirst: Descubre curiosidades sobre uno de los partidos más esperados de la temporada
articles.summary: Raúl González Blanco dio sus primeros pasos en el mundo del fútbol en el conjunto rojiblanco
articles.body: Raúl González Blanco es una de las mayores leyendas del Real Madrid. Con más de 15 títulos en su palmarés y más de 300 goles en su casillero personal, el madrileño se postuló como uno de los mejores canteranos de todos los tiempos del club de Chamartín. Pero lo que no sabe mucha gente, es que la historia del ‘7’ blanco pudo haber sido muy distinta. Ya que, Raúl dio sus primeros pasos en el mundo del fútbol en el Atlético de Madrid, eterno rival del cuadro vikingo. El legendario '7' blanco, debutó como profesional ante el Zaragoza. Tras el encuentro contra los maños, donde no pudo ver puerta y estuvo un tanto desacertado, llegaría su segunda oportunidad ante un rival muy especial para él, el Atlético de Madrid. En aquella noche de noviembre de 1994, con tan solo 17 años, Raúl González Blanco dejó su primera huella en la historia del Real Madrid. El delantero se convirtió en el jugador más joven en marcar en un derbi, récord que todavía sigue vigente. Era su debut en el Bernabéu y tardó 26 minutos en dinamitar el partido: provocó el penalti del 1-0 de Michel y asistió a Zamorano en el 2-0. Su gol llegaría antes del descanso para poner el 3-1 en el marcador. Fue a pase de Laudrup, quien dirigió una contra por la izquierda y conectó con Raúl en la semiluna del área. El ya ‘7’ no desaprovechó el 'regalo' y clavó su zurdazo en la escuadra de Diego. De una leyenda madridista a otra. En el escalafón de los realizadores más veteranos se sitúa Alfredo Di Stéfano. El atacante argentino le hizo un tanto al Atlético de Madrid en el curso 1963-64 a la edad de 37 años y 143 días, durante un encuentro que concluyó con goleada por 5-1 a favor de los locales.

articles.title: Los seis derbis con más goles de la historia: de los 50 a 2025
articles.standfirst: Estos son los partidos entre el Real Madrid y el Atlético de Madrid con más goles de la historia
articles.summary: Estos son los cinco partidos entre el Real Madrid y el Atlético de Madrid con más goles de la historia
articles.body: El derbi madrileño ha sido, durante más de un siglo, escenario de rivalidades calientes y goles en cascada. Ests son los cinco enfrentamientos entre Real Madrid y Atlético de Madrid que, oficialmente, quedan como los de mayor número de tantos anotados en un mismo partido. Aunque se trataba de un partido amistoso de pretemporada en Nueva Jersey, este encuentro se convirtió en uno de los más recordados por la abultada cifra de goles, hasta 10. Desde el primer minuto, el Atlético mostró un despliegue ofensivo impresionante, con Diego Costa como gran protagonista al firmar cuatro tantos. Los hinchas rojiblancos disfrutaron de un verdadero espectáculo de goles y transiciones rápidas, mientras que el Real Madrid, pese a intentar reaccionar, no pudo contener los ataques rivales y perdió por una diferencia abultada. En un Metropolitano abarrotado, el Atlético de Madrid protagonizó una tarde inolvidable frente al Real Madrid, imponiéndose 6-3 en un derbi que quedó grabado en la historia. Desde el inicio, el conjunto rojiblanco mostró un fútbol dinámico y decidido, marcando el ritmo y controlando los espacios con autoridad. Larbi Ben Barek brilló como figura del encuentro, anotando goles decisivos y guiando al equipo hacia una victoria contundente. El Real Madrid se impuso al Atlético de Madrid por 6-3 en el derbi disputado el 13 de mayo de 1950. Desde temprano, los blancos tomaron la delantera en el marcador y mantuvieron la ventaja a lo largo del encuentro, mientras el Atlético intentaba reaccionar sin éxito. Pahiño destacó como uno de los goleadores del Real Madrid, contribuyendo de manera decisiva a la victoria. Este choque oficial, disputado en Arabia Saudí, fue un auténtico maratón de emociones. El Real Madrid y el Atlético se alternaron el dominio del partido en varias fases, con goles de ida y vuelta que mantenían a la afición al borde del asiento. La prórroga fue decisiva, y finalmente los blancos lograron imponerse 5-3. En el antiguo Chamartín, este derbi de los años 60 presentó un fútbol abierto y ofensivo, característico de la época. Real Madrid y Atlético se alternaron en el dominio del partido, con constantes cambios en el marcador que mantuvieron la tensión hasta el último minuto, con doblete de Puskas incluído. La victoria final del Real Madrid quedó grabada en la memoria de los aficionados y se recuerda como uno de los mejores derbis de la historia. El derbi de la presente temporada reunió todos los ingredientes: la visita de Xabi Alonso al Metropolitano, el gol de Mbappé y la remontada del Atlético. El conjunto colchonero se adelantó con un gol de Le Normand, pero llegó la reacción blanca con sendos tantos de Arda Guler y Mbappé. Antes del descanso igualó Sorloth y en la segunda parte Julián Álvarez por partida doble y Griezmann redondearon una tarde mágica.

articles.title: Deco: "La renovación de Raphinha hasta 2030 está encaminada, y también las de Bernal y Xavi Espart"
articles.standfirst: El Director Deportivo interviene en la Asamblea Ordinaria
articles.summary: El Director Deportivo interviene en la Asamblea Ordinaria
articles.body: Deco intervino este sábado en la Asamblea General Ordinaria del Barcelona 2026 para exponer la gestión deportiva de la entidad. El ejecutivo culé aseguró que se mantienen en la misma línea de trabajo de los últimos años y se mostró satisfecho con la labor realizada. "Los 90 minutos que pasan en el campo no son casualidad", aseguró. También desveló que las ampliaciones de Raphinha, Marc Bernal y Xavi Espart están muy encaminadas. La del atacante brasileño, que impulsó ayer, será de un año más: hasta 2030. El Director Deportivo empezó su informe ante los socios compromisarios repasando los cambios en la plantilla. Se refirió a las altas (Gordon, Adeyemi, Cancelo y Livakovic); a las bajas, tanto de los cedidos (Ter Stegen, Casadó y Araujo), como de los traspasados (Ansu Fati, Iñaki Peña, Ferran Torres, Jofre Torrents, Tommy Marqués, Héctor Fort, Álvaro Cortés, Guille Fernández y Toni Fernández) como los que finalizaron contrato (Rashford y Lewandowski); y también valoró las renovaciones (Fermín, Christensen, De Jong, Eric García, Hamza y Flick y su staff) concretadas. Pero Deco, adelantó, además, que hay otras ampliaciones muy avanzadas. "La renovación de Raphinha hasta 2030 está muy encaminada, y las de Marc Bernal y Xavi Espart, también", desveló. Los contactos con el brasileño se intensificaron y avanzaron, según apuntó, ayer viernes por la tarde. Posteriormente, Deco explicitó que el valor de mercado del primer equipo de la temporada 26-27 es de 1.260 millones de euros, 524 más que en el inicio de la 21-22 y 180 más respecto a la 34-35. Del valor del presente curso, además, 583 corresponden a jugadores formados en La Masia, que representa el 46 por ciento del total. "Tenemos el valor de plantilla más alto del mundo", aseguró el excentrocampista. En relación al balance del mercado, el ejecutivo azulgrana señaló en su exposición que las compras ascendieron a 181 millones y las ventas a 72 (precios netos, no beneficios). "No cambiaremos nuestra estrategia de trabajo ni nuestro objetivo deportivo, que es ganar todos los títulos. Además, queremos seguir contando con los jóvenes de La Masia", señaló Deco como algunos de los puntos que sigue el área deportiva en su hoja de ruta. Por último, Rafa Yuste también valoró y destacó la gestión del área deportiva, destacando a todos los profesionales, especialmente a Flick, Deco y Bojan.

articles.title: Everything Pete Golding Said About 'Emotion,' Concern vs. Lane Kiffin, LSU in Ole Miss Revenge Game
articles.summary: Ole Miss head football coach Pete Golding discussed his feelings regarding Saturday night's massive SEC clash with the LSU Tigers, who are led by former Ole Miss head coach Lane Kiffin.
articles.body:
Ole Miss head football coach Pete Golding discussed his feelings regarding Saturday night's massive SEC clash with the LSU Tigers, who are led by former Ole Miss head coach Lane Kiffin.

During an appearance Saturday morning on ESPN College GameDay on Saturday morning, Golding talked about his concerns and his goals for the game.

"I think it's the intentional focus piece of doing my job," Golding said. "And I think progression teaching is so important, and I got to go back in that moment, 'Alright, what's my lineup assignment key? What's my primary key, my secondary key? What's my footwork?' And [Nick Saban] always talked about, it's fine to have emotion, you just can't become emotional, and we all start making bad decisions. I learned that from him all the time. So, I think that's there. I worry about a little bit pregame, like don't play the game too early. You don't want to be the loudest guy in the bar, that ain't it. Let's focus and let's do our job.

Buzz: Kiffin Wants to 'Embarrass' Ole Miss 😈

"So, we'll see. I think some guys have been in these big moments, they'll be okay. I just don't want them to have to press. We're not asking you to do anything you haven't done before. You don't have to play perfect. We're not perfect. We're not going to be perfect. We've got to be at our best, whatever that looks like. We have to make the least amount of mistakes than the other team. Let's out-physical the other team, Let's go out and let loose and play football. This is what you do it for."

Saturday's game would be a huge one under normal circumstances with Ole Miss ranked No. 8 in the nation and LSU ranked No. 7, but the emotions figure to be running even higher than usual at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford, Mississippi, due to the fact that Kiffin made the decision to leave Ole Miss for LSU prior to last season's College Football Playoff.

Although Kiffin lobbied publicly to stay on as Ole Miss' head coach through the CFP last season, the school instead promoted Golding from defensive coordinator to head coach.

There were doubts about the Rebels' chances of success in the CFP after making such a significant change, but the team beat both Tulane and Georgia in the playoffs before falling 31-27 to Miami in a semifinal nail-biter.

Golding is now in the midst of his first full season as Ole Miss' head coach, and the Rebels are off to a strong, 2-0 start with wins over No. 23 Louisville and Charlotte.

Ole Miss returned several key players from last season's CFP semifinals squad, including quarterback Trinidad Chambliss and running back Kewan Lacy.

Chambliss, Lacy and many other members of the Ole Miss squad played under Kiffin during his six-year tenure at the school, plus Kiffin brought multiple players and coaches with him from Ole Miss to LSU.

Because of that, there will be no shortage of familiarity between the two teams, and it should add even more intrigue to an already massive game.

During his College GameDay appearance (h/t Sam Sklar of the Clarion Ledger ), Golding laid out his expectations for an LSU side he is familiar with, along with what he believes his players need to do in order to get the upper hand.

"I think it's a combination of really three things," Golding said. "To your point, I think disguises are first because, as you know, when we start changing calls, getting all 11 guys on the same page isn't always perfect. So, I think the disguise piece of that is really important early in the downs.

"But also, I think it's got to be on the players to be able to go kill [the play] on the field. With their Nike and their Reebok, their fake look and the real look, they try to get you. We got to do that on the field with our players or at least we can get in one call and out of another call. But from a green dot standpoint, it's all 11 guys are on the same page. It's not from me on the sideline. So, if they screw it up, all 11 are screwing up on the same call. We'll be OK if we do that, but we got to be able to change the picture on them. But we also got to be able to get out of certain things that they know you're in, so you don't get the beaters."

Even if Golding and Kiffin would prefer to put the emphasis on the players and what happens on the field, it is clear that Ole Miss fans are harboring ill will toward Kiffin.

He was booed mercilessly by the Rebels fans in attendance at ESPN College GameDay on Saturday morning, and the boos will likely be even louder when he runs onto the field prior to the start of Saturday night's game.

The elements are present for both teams to have some added motivation, but none of them should need it since beating a top team and taking a massive step toward SEC championship and CFP contention should be motivation enough.

articles.title: Mourinho lanza varios dardos y una oda los derbis
articles.standfirst: "Es muy difícil que se oiga algo bueno del Real Madrid", asegura el entrenador del Madrid
articles.summary: "Es muy difícil que se oiga algo bueno del Real Madrid", asegura el entrenador del Madrid
articles.body: José Mourinho sitúa al derbi en la rutina de los tres puntos en juego de cada semana. Pero en la rueda de prensa previa al derbi se refirió varias veces al contenido cultural que tienen estos partidos. Los ha vivido en Lisboa, Oporto, Londres, Milán, Manchester, Estambul y ahora se reencuentra con el de Madrid. Tanta referencia al contenido cultural de los derbis llevaba a preguntarle con cuál de ellos se queda. "Es difícil decirlo, porque cuando vistes la camiseta de un club, pasas a sentir como aficionado. No hay un derbi que vas por la calle la semana previa y alguien no te dice ‘vamos a matar a la Juve...’, o a quien sea. O te aíslas y no tienes contacto con el mundo exterior. El que más me ha sorprendido por lo inesperado es el Milan-Inter, porque pensaba que había mucho no, pero un poco de odio y me ha sorprendido que son amigos, tienen buena relación. El odio está un poco más al norte. Yo veía a una señora y a un señor con sus camisetas, diferentes, por la calle. O un padre y un niño. En Portugal eso es imposible... ¡Y en Turquía no te hablo!". En una rueda de prensa suave, el entrenador del Madrid sí lanzó dardos. En varias direcciones. "Histórica y culturalmente, el Real Madrid no puede estar comparándose con nadie. Y por esto no me voy a comparar con ninguno. Hablo de nosotros y lo hago sin problema, de problemas y virtudes. A pesar de que cada vez es más difícil escuchar algo positivo del Real Madrid. Pero seguimos nuestro trabajo con humildad. Sin ningún problema de ser consciente de nuestros problemas. Pero también sabedores de las cosas muy buenas que también tenemos en el equipo". Un mensjaje que cargó de contenido: "En los tres partidos que hemos llegado a los minutos finales necesitando marcar para ganar o empatar, hemos terminado con una fuerza física, psicológica y una entrega y determinación... se puede decir claramente: no es normal ir 0-2 al Elche y que te empaten en el minuto 80. Pero tampoco es normal que te empaten y en unos minutos el equipo cambie, tenga una, otra, otra... y marque y gane. Con el Betis pasó igual. Este equipo tiene, además de calidad, una fuerza con un significado muy grande. Que es la fuerza de un grupo. Y esto meda confianza. Esto es una maratón, no una autopista. Cuando se habló de derbi, Mourinho no dudó en colocar al Atlético de Madrid como candidato al título. Y cuando apareció Simeone eligió la palabra respeto: "A lo largo de la carrera decimos tantas tonterías que si vas atrás, no hay uno de nosotros a salvo. O cosas influenciado por el momento... o estratégicamente. A mí me llamaron para hablar en el documental de Simeone y no lo dudé ni un minuto. El sabe qué pienso de él. Lo primero es el respeto. Somos rivales, pero compañeros de guerra. El asunto de las camisetas de apoyo a Ceuta, Mourinho se limitó a un "yo solo hablo de fútbol". Y otra pregunta asegurada era la de las desconexiones que el Madrid sufre con una constancia inquietante. "No sé si conseguiré que el equipo salga al 100%, pero es mi intención y la de mis jugadores. Pero no sé si lo conseguiré. Llevamos muchos partidos seguidos, pero hemos conseguido corregir algunas cosas, es un proceso. Si hay clubes que entrenan durante tres, cuatro o cinco días seguidos... si se habla siempre de evolución, imagina nosotros, que en estos pocos meses ya hemos jugado siete u ocho partidos oficiales. Hay que mejorar. Pero también conseguir resultados. Y estamos trabajando. Tenemos mucha confianza, pero también sabemos que debemos trabajar". Y para acabar, una reflexión arbitral: "¿Lo de los penaltis la semana pasada? Ya es tarde. Ha pasado una jornada. Podríamos hablar de por qué el Elche acabó con once. Pero si entramos en eso... Es un poco extraño que hace una semana ya supiéramos el árbitro de mañana. Yo prefiero decir que si le han nombrado, es porque tiene calidad. Experiencia suficiente para un partido de esta dimensión emocional. No me gusta hablar de árbitros antes del partido. Después ya veremos. Pero antes, tiene toda mi confianza".

articles.title: Lane Kiffin Signs Go Viral as Ole Miss Fans Troll LSU HC in Photos, Videos During 'College GameDay'
articles.summary: Ole Miss fans got creative when welcoming former Rebels head coach Lane Kiffin back to Oxford ahead of Saturday's rivalry matchup against LSU.

Ole Miss fans got creative when welcoming former Rebels head coach Lane Kiffin back to Oxford ahead of Saturday's rivalry matchup against LSU.

Logan Media Network's Brad Logan shared photos and videos of some of the Kiffin-themed signs on the display for Saturday morning's taping of ESPN's College GameDay.

Saturday will mark Kiffin's first game against Ole Miss since leaving the program ahead of last winter's College Football Playoff run.

Kiffin prepared his team for the matchup by having LSU fans heckle players with fake signs before the trip to Oxford.

Kickoff between No. 7 LSU and No. 8 Ole Miss is scheduled for 7:30 p.m. ET at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium.

articles.title: Watch Lane Kiffin React to 'Gaslighting' as Ole Miss Fans Relentlessly Boo LSU HC in New Video
articles.summary: LSU head football coach Lane Kiffin attempted to downplay the storyline surrounding his return to Oxford, Mississippi, prior to Saturday night's road game against Ole Miss.
articles.body:
LSU head football coach Lane Kiffin attempted to downplay the storyline surrounding his return to Oxford, Mississippi, prior to Saturday night's road game against Ole Miss.

Appearing Saturday morning on ESPN College GameDay via satellite, Kiffin was booed heavily by the Ole Miss faithful when shown on the screen. Despite that, Kiffin put the focus on the players who will be competing in the game between the No. 7 Tigers and No. 8 Rebels.

"It's not about me," Kiffin said. "Both teams have great players, great coaches. Have a lot of respect for their program. So, this is about the players performing really well tonight in a really awesome matchup of two top-10 teams, national game of the week. So, both programs should be really excited."

Kiffin continued by stressing the importance of focus and execution rather than getting caught up in the emotions of Saturday's game, while also making mention of College GameDay "gaslighting" the Ole Miss fans.

"Not to play on emotion. Obviously, it's going to be there," Kiffin said. "There's going to be some of it, especially for some of these coaches coming back, but most importantly, some players coming back, but to play on execution. This will be a really competitive game for a long period of time with a lot of plays. And so, you've got to really stay focused and not listen to all of the noise and all the chatter as you enter into the stadium. But thanks guys, I really appreciate you gaslighting them this morning."

Kiffin suggested he was fully aware of what to expect Saturday, and despite the vitriol being sent his way, he expressed his belief that it's a positive thing for college football.

"We just tried to do everything to simulate the game, simulate the day," Kiffin said. "Whether it's having a mock game for the Clemson game or this situation, having people heckle them just so they get used to it so they try not to react when they get into that setting today. Because there's going to be a lot of emotion all throughout the stadium, obviously. You're feeling that right now, and a lot of excitement. I look at it differently. I look at it as what an awesome thing for college football to have this game, have this much energy, have two states behind their programs like this from governors to everybody. I mean, this is college football."

Kiffin decided to spurn Ole Miss by taking the LSU head coaching job prior to last season's College Football Playoff, resulting in Ole Miss replacing him with Pete Golding, who led the Rebels to the CFP semifinals.

With Golding at the helm for his first full season as head coach, Ole Miss returns a great roster led by quarterback Trinidad Chambliss and Kewan Lacy.

Meanwhile, Kiffin is looking to get LSU back on track on the heels of the Tigers going a disappointing 7-6 last season and having not reached the CFP since 2019.

LSU does look to be an entirely different team under Kiffin, as the Tigers blew out Clemson 51-10 in Week 1 and followed it up with a 45-14 win over Louisiana Tech in Week 2.

Kiffin has the LSU offense humming, as quarterback Sam Leavitt has accounted for seven total touchdowns through two games, including five on the ground.

A road game against Ole Miss and its rowdy fans will be an entirely different challenge for Kiffin and Co., though, especially since Golding is a defensive coach with an intimate knowledge of the type of offense Kiffin likes to run.

As much as Kiffin tried to deflect it, the crowd could be a very real factor in Saturday night's game as well, especially in terms of impacting LSU's ability to communicate on offense.

Regardless of the many storylines attached to the game, including Kiffin's return to Oxford, it should be a spectacular contest featuring two of the best teams in college football.

There are no guarantees for either team coming out of it whether they win or lose, but the winner will undoubtedly have a leg up when it comes to potentially vying for a berth in the SEC Championship Game and the CFP.

articles.body: El Rayo Vallecano se va con un punto al parón, antes de la vuelta a casa. El cuadro franjirrojo consiguió empatar el tanto de Ante Budimir por medio de su hombre 'gol' Sergio Camello y ya tiene la mirada puesta en ese encuentro ante el Athletic Club del 10 de octubre que se jugará en Vallecas. Beñat San José habló con los medios tras el encuentro. Valoración del partido: "En la segunda parte hemos empezado muy bien. Al final ellos también aprietan y son buenos. El final ha sido muy intenso. Cuando hemos estado muy bien, podríamos haber remontado hacia la victoria. Hemos conseguido el empate que es bueno y más cuando vas perdiendo. En la primera parte también hemos estado bien, pero ellos han entrado más intensos. Me da rabia el gol que nos han anotado. Es un punto que suma". Público rayista desplazado: "La afición es un espectáculo, les hemos escuchado y nos han ayudado. Lo notamos mucho. Es espectacular, proactiva, te anima todo el rato y te empuja. Te hace tener el sentimiento de pertenencia muy rápidamente". Sergio Camello y su no inclusión en la lista de De la Fuente: "No ha ido, pero yo estoy convencido de que si sigue así, en un futuro irá. Hay nueves muy buenos y que esté Camello entre ellos es importante para él y para nosotros. Estamos encantados con él". Parón: "Mis sensaciones son muy buenas. Estas semanas nos ayudarán a recuperar a la gente que está tocada y también para pulir conceptos. Descansaremos lo justo y necesario porque necesitamos recuperar, pero también aumentaremos las cargas físicas. Veremos si podemos meter un partido amistoso. Estas semanas nos servirán para trabajar duro". Terreno de juego: "Me han garantizado que el terreno de juego está bien. Nuestra intención es entrenar allí. articles.title: Sir Jim Ratcliffe: Man Utd co-owner 'must go' says Muslim fan group
articles.summary: The Manchester United Muslim Supporters Club says United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe "must go" after he spoke out against immigration and said the country was "on the slide".
articles.body:
The Manchester United Muslim Supporters group says club co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe "must go" after he spoke out against immigration levels and said the country was "on the slide".

Billionaire Ratcliffe, who is one of Britain's richest people and founder of petrochemical giant Ineos, made the comments in an interview with the BBC on Saturday.

Ratcliffe said the UK was in decline because of a combination of high taxes and high immigration.

He has previously apologised for "offending some people" with his language after saying the UK had been "colonised by immigrants".

At the time, in February, United responded by saying the club "prides itself" on being "inclusive", while BBC Sport cited a source familiar with the Glazer family as understanding the club's majority shareholders were "horrified" by his initial remarks and saw them as showing "disregard for their ownership".

"We condemned those comments then," said the Manchester United Muslim Supporters Club (MUMSC) on Saturday, in a statement of no confidence in the club's ownership.

"He [Ratcliffe] subsequently apologised for his choice of language. We hoped a lesson had been learned. Clearly, it has not.

"This week, Sir Jim has again placed immigration and people receiving benefits at the centre of his explanation for Britain's problems, arguing that nobody is 'tough enough' to deal with either.

"We find these latest comments deeply disappointing and completely unacceptable."

Ratcliffe campaigned for a Leave vote in the 2016 European Union referendum and has been a tax resident in Monaco since 2020.

He acquired a 27.7% stake in Man Utd in 2024, and has since restructured the organisation, overseeing 450 redundancies, overhauling senior management and sacking two managers.

MUMSC highlighted that United's "players, staff, stewards, security teams and supporters come from different countries, cultures, ethnicities, religions and backgrounds".

The group added: "Manchester United would not be Manchester United without them. That diversity isn't a weakness of Manchester United. It is part of Manchester United."

In the statement, the MUMSC also called on the Glazer family to go.

MUMSC said its members were among the club's fans who hoped Ratcliffe's arrival "would finally signal meaningful change" after the Glazer family had "presided over Manchester United's decline".

However, the group pointed to "higher ticket prices" and "a stadium allowed to deteriorate", along with "a football team that continues to fall further behind where Manchester United should be", among their concerns which "now extend beyond the pitch".

Manchester United entered the weekend sitting 13th in the Premier League after gaining four points from their first four Premier League games, and they were knocked out of the Carabao Cup on Wednesday with a 3-2 home defeat by Brighton.

"After years of decline, broken promises and repeated failure, Manchester United Muslim Supporters' Club has lost confidence in the current ownership structure of Manchester United Football Club," MUMSC concluded.

"Enough is enough. It is time for change. The Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe must go."

articles.title: UEFA defends policy after rejecting Ireland’s request not to play Israel
articles.summary: UEFA responds after Ireland’s football association says its request to avoid future pairings with Israel was ⁠⁠rejected.
articles.body:
UEFA has said that decisions on whether national teams should be kept apart in ⁠⁠competition draws are made ⁠⁠on a case-by-case basis and guided primarily by security considerations, after the Republic of Ireland’s football association said its request to avoid future pairings with Israel had been ⁠⁠rejected.

Football Association of Ireland chief executive David Courell said on Friday that it had asked UEFA if the Republic of Ireland and Israel could be separated in future draws ⁠⁠after being paired in February’s Nations League draw.

They are due to meet in that competition on September 27 and October 4.

European football’s governing body said requests to stop teams being drawn against each other are considered individually.

“Decisions to avoid certain teams being ‌‌drawn against each other are made taking into consideration several factors, especially conditions between the two countries leading to structural risks for security,” UEFA said in a statement on Saturday.

“UEFA handles every situation very carefully on its own merits and monitors all facts and developments.”

Courell told reporters the FAI had been informed that such an arrangement would not be possible because Ireland and Israel had “never been in direct conflict”.

The Israel Football Association also responded ⁠⁠to Courell’s remarks, questioning whether a formal request had been ⁠⁠made to UEFA.

“The question should be directed at UEFA: was there an official inquiry or request regarding this matter, or is this merely another inconsequential statement?” IFA head of communications Shlomi Barzel told the Reuters news agency.

“Since we long ago ⁠⁠stopped getting worked up over statements detached from reality, we are focusing on high-quality professional preparations to achieve our goals on ⁠⁠the pitch.”

The fixtures have been controversial in Ireland amid the ⁠⁠conflict in the Middle East.

Last November, members of the FAI voted overwhelmingly for its board to request that UEFA should suspend the IFA from European competitions, while in May, leading Irish footballers and celebrities joined in a ‌‌campaign for a boycott of Ireland’s home Nations League fixture.

Ireland’s designated home match on October 4 is due to be played behind closed doors in Backa Topola, Serbia, instead of ‌‌Dublin, ‌‌while Irish fans will not receive tickets for Israel’s designated home fixture in Debrecen, Hungary, the previous weekend.
