articles.title: How Much Money Lane Kiffin's LSU Could Be Fined by SEC for Sam Leavitt Injury Report
articles.summary: LSU coach Lane Kiffin could be risking financial penalties should the SEC rule he violated rules by listing quarterback Sam Leavitt earlier this week as "doubtful" to play Saturday against Ole Miss.
articles.body:
LSU coach Lane Kiffin could be risking financial penalties should the SEC rule he violated rules by listing quarterback Sam Leavitt earlier this week as "doubtful" to play Saturday against Ole Miss.

Leavitt was listed as doubtful Wednesday and upgraded to questionable Thursday before he was removed from LSU's injury report Friday night.

The SEC rulebook warns of penalties in case of "failure to provide accurate and timely information on the availability report."

Buzz: Ole Miss Skeptical of LSU QB's Status 🤨

Financial penalties for football programs range for $25,000 for a first offense to $50,000 for second violations and $100,000 for any subsequent issues, according to the SEC.

Separate financial penalties could also be leveled to head coaches involved in rule violations, per the SEC.

Kiffin said Saturday Leavitt had "a scare" earlier this week but later "had a great recovery."

"Sam's doing great. Early in the week, he had a scare there, he didn't practice," Kiffin said in a Saturday morning appearance on ESPN's Pat McAfee Show. "But he's had a great recovery, worked really hard, and he's ready to go."

ESPN's Alex Scarborough reported "sources on the Ole Miss staff told ESPN's Pete Thamel on Thursday morning that they weren't convinced that Leavitt's appearance on the availability report was sincere."

Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said in a Thursday appearance on McAfee's show Kiffin had texted him before the injury report was released to say Leavitt was "out."

"I'm like, 'Yeah, buddy, I bet he is,'" Golding laughed. "I've been around here a lot of Wednesdays with you, man, for three and a half years. I said, 'I think our first one, we had 42 guys on the first-ever SEC injury report on a Wednesday.' I was like, 'Yeah, man. See you Saturday.'"

Kiffin further raised questions in his Thursday evening radio show , during which he discussed the upcoming Ole Miss matchup but did not address Leavitt's injury status.

Both teams are undefeated heading into Saturday's matchup, although Leavitt is looking to put together a more consistent performance after throwing a trio of first-half interceptions in last Saturday's win over Louisiana Tech.

Leavitt will be expected to start when No. 7 LSU takes on No. 8 Ole Miss at 7:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Ramis: "Hemos estado poco precisos y con algo de miedo"
articles.standfirst: El técnico rojillo valoró el aspecto defensivo del equipo, pero no el ofensivo
articles.summary: El técnico rojillo valoró el aspecto defensivo del equipo, pero no el ofensivo
articles.body: El entrenador de Osasuna, Luis Miguel Ramis, afirmó este sábado, tras empatar 1-1 con el Rayo Vallecano, que su equipo estuvo "poco preciso y con algo de miedo" ante el conjunto madrileño. "Queríamos los tres puntos, pero el empate es justo. Nos hemos enfrentado a un buen equipo, con mucha capacidad de atraer, combinar, y lo hemos contrarrestado bien. El orden defensivo ha estado bien, otra cosa ha sido la ofensiva, donde hemos estado muy imprecisos", expuso Ramis. Sobre la lesión de Raúl Moro, Ramis comentó que su futbolista "no tiene la continuidad que necesitamos y cada vez que acumula carga le aparece una lesión muscular. Lo peor es que cuando ve que tiene continuidad al final llega esto y es un paso atrás. Tiene la ventaja de estas tres semanas para tener un poco de adelante, y espero tenerlo en dos partidos listo". "Tenemos jugadores que nos van a aportar más recursos. Ha sido muy exigente estos dos bloques de partidos y nos ha penalizado en el plano de lesiones y a la hora detener margen de maniobra para poder manejar con cambios desde el banquillo alguna situación", continuó. Analizó lo visto frente al Rayo Vallecano, asegurando haberse dado mejoras: "El equipo, poco a poco, va a ir cogiendo confianza. Estas semanas pasadas, las tres derrotas, en el plano ofensivo, habíamos tenido minutos bastantes buenos, pero en el plano defensivo estábamos mal. Hoy hemos mejorado mucho en esa organización defensiva, pero hemos estado poco precisos y con algo de miedo. Nos falta desempolvarnos ese miedo y que el campo mejore, porque tiene mucha arena". "Hemos puesto lo que creíamos que nos podía dar esas piernas que 100 % que necesitábamos para el partido y lo hemos tenido. No hemos bajado energía", comentó sobre los 7 cambios en el once respecto a la alineación del Metropolitano.

articles.title: Tottenham 2-3 Aston Villa: No sign of recovery from struggling Spurs
articles.summary: Tottenham look no closer to solving their problems as they slip to a home defeat by Aston Villa to add to their Premier League misery.
articles.body:
The closer Tottenham went to scoring the more it seemed likely they would concede.

"Too fragile" was how boss Roberto de Zerbi described his side after the 3-2 defeat by Aston Villa .

Comfortable and on top until Johan Manzambi's scrappy opener for the visitors - while Spurs were temporarily down to 10 men as Micky van de Ven had treatment - they never recovered.

It only got worse as goals from Nicolas Jackson and Emi Buendia put the visitors 3-0 up.

De Zerbi's men now go into a three-week international break still waiting for a first Premier League win this season as Conor Gallagher and Jan Paul van Hecke's late goals - the club's first in the league - were of little consolation.

In the bottom three after spending over £300m in the summer there appears to be no end in sight to Spurs' struggles.

Tottenham have failed to win any of their last 36 Premier League matches when conceding first so the writing was on the wall at half-time.

They dominated the opening 20 minutes and Villa keeper Zion Suzuki denied Savio and Archie Gray but, without a goal, they were always going to be vulnerable at the other end.

And so, in first-half injury time, a Villa goal was almost inevitable.

Andy Robertson tried to stop a corner but only gifted the ball to John McGinn and, after Boubacar Kamara's effort, Manzambi prodded in from close range. It added the insult to Van de Ven's injury, a blow to the face that kept him off the pitch.

Some Tottenham fans missed the goal as they headed for their half-time refreshments but several thousand did not bother to stay until the end.

They streamed out of the stands after Buendia's brilliant 25-yard bullet found the top corner in the 79th minute, missing Gallagher and Van Hecke's late efforts.

De Zerbi said: "My focus is why we concede the first goal with 10 players, we can stay stronger, communicate more and more, defend in a compact way.

"I put [Rodrigo] Bentancur as a centre-back in that minute and Mateus Fernandes as a midfielder. If we have a red card we can play 70 minutes with 10 players.

"In the second half we scored the goal with [Mohammed] Kudus, offside, I don't know if some players lost energy but we conceded an unacceptable goal. We knew this season Aston Villa are playing 86% more long balls than last season.

"We had many meetings [about it] and we have to explain another game like Newcastle where we played the first half well and then we lose. It's my responsibility.

"I take my responsibility but in that moment of the game we have to defend, we have to defend compact, the leaders have to be leaders.

"I am very sad and frustrated with the performance. We cannot lose this game in this way. The second goal we conceded was incredible."

"Sacked in the morning" chanted the Villa fans to De Zerbi who, at times, looked out of ideas once his side fell 2-0 behind.

It was Tottenham 's worst start to a top-flight season since 2008-09, when they also had two points after five games.

Juande Ramos was dismissed as manager after three more defeats before Harry Redknapp lifted them up to eighth. Spurs have also now gone five league games without a win at the start of a season for the first time since 1986.

Former Brighton striker Glenn Murray, however, says De Zerbi needs time.

"He is trying to build something, it will take time," he told BBC's Final Score. "Taking the emotion out of it, looking at the stats, they have had more shots in three of the past four games, more possession and more touches in the opposition box.

"They are positives, be patient, the metrics are there to say he will turn it around. They need to be patient with Roberto De Zerbi, with all the signings, it takes time to gel and get to know each other."

A decisive moment came when Kudus thought he had levelled on the hour, but Robertson was ruled just offside having delivered the cross. Seven minutes later Jackson scored from Suzuki's long launch downfield and it was game over.

Villa's rebuild, the club committing to spending more than £250m was out of necessity because of their own high-profile exits.

There was an expectation change was forthcoming and the Europa League winners were always going to go through a period of transition.

But a first league victory was vital for them too after three defeats in their opening four games.

While Villa look in better shape as new players settle, Spurs have thrown money at their problems after two relegation battles, but are no closer to solving them.

Sandro Tonali, the £100m midfielder from Newcastle , was overshadowed by Villa's tenacious skipper McGinn - a £2.75m buy from Hibs eight years ago.

Brazil winger Savio was denied three times by the impressive Suzuki but faded, while Omar Marmoush was signed to bring goals, but provided nothing.

De Zerbi added: "I didn't speak with the players [afterwards], I didn't want to say anything. The players who go to the national team, they have to play and work.

"The others, [James] Maddison, Gallagher, [Dominic] Solanke, Tosin [Adarabioyo, [Marcos] Senesi, Savio have to work more because their physical condition, I didn't like in this game."

Villa survive late Spurs fightback to earn first Premier League win

Manzambi catches eye as Villa beat Spurs - player ratings

Spurs have overpaid for every player - Cole

Former Chelsea and England midfielder Joe Cole questioned Tottenham 's transfer business after their spend of around £302m.

After Tonali, £85m went on bringing in Mateus Fernandes from West Ham. The Portuguese midfielder was subbed at half-time and De Zerbi said he "didn't like" Fernandes' performance, while £75m was spent on Savio from Manchester City.

Marmoush will cost £60m once his loan becomes permanent but Spurs need their big-money buys to prove their worth and perform sooner rather than later.

"Spurs are dominant, chances, and you felt the tension growing - all of a sudden Spurs were just wanting to get to half-time. Once you defend with anxiety, things happen," Cole told TNT.

"When these things go against you, they go against you, Van de Ven going off was a factor, they didn't deal with it well, when you are anxious you make rash decisions.

"Villa defended well but didn't deserve to go in a goal up, and then this place deflated.

"They are not picking up points, a club flirting with relegation two years in a row, I feel they have overpaid for every player they bought this summer - you can't rule them out from being in and around the relegation battle."

De Zerbi, though, defended their summer window despite their current malaise.

"I am happy with the squad but the market was long, the situation changed many times," he said.

"There was also financial fair play and we have to respect that. We didn't sell the players we thought there was a possibility to sell.

"The club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players. If we didn't make any different decisions it was because we couldn't."

articles.title: Estupor en la Federación por la solicitud de Interior de cancelar el amistoso Sub 20 de España en Ceuta
articles.standfirst: No entiende que el Gobierno quiera prohibir este partido cuando no hay trabas para que se jueguen los encuentros de LaLiga Hypermotion en el Alfonso Murube
articles.summary: No entiende que el Gobierno quiera prohibir este partido cuando no hay trabas para que se jueguen los encuentros de LaLiga Hypermotion en el Alfonso Murube
articles.body: El Ministerio del Interior pide cancelar el partido de la selección española de fútbol Sub-20 en Ceuta por la "presión migratoria existente y el contexto de conflictividad social que trae consigo", según informa el diario El Mundo. Bajo estos argumentos, en los que se elude en todo momento calificar de invasión territorial lo ocurrido, el departamento que dirige el ministro Fernando Grande-Marlaska se opone radicalmente a la celebración del encuentro amistoso fijado para el próximo 30 de septiembre contra México. Este partido ha sido organizado por la Real Federación Española de Fútbol como muestra de apoyo a los ceutíes en la situación más complicada de su historia. Argumenta el Ministerio del Interior que "es ineludible considerar la situación excepcional que actualmente atraviesa la ciudad autónoma como consecuencia de la presión migratoria existente". Al tiempo que evita mencionar la existencia de una violación de nuestra frontera que tiene en jaque a la ciudad norteafricana, se limita a la existencia de "un clima de tensión en la vía pública y, especialmente, en el entorno donde se encuentra ubicado el estadio". De esta forma reconoce que no está en condiciones de garantizar la seguridad del encuentro. Se queja además Interior de que el estadio Alfonso Murube carece de Unidad de Control Organizativo (UCO) "pese a tratarse de un recinto en el que se disputan competiciones de carácter profesional" y añade que "su ausencia adquiere especial relevancia en el presente caso, al poder resultar necesario suplir dicha carencia mediante recursos y medios adicionales". En la Federación existe estupor por esta iniciativa al considerar que el Gobierno no permite que España juegue en Ceuta mientras que no existe ninguna prohibición para que se disputen partidos de LaLiga Hypermotion como el que se disputa mañana en el Alfonso Murube ante el Valladolid.

articles.title: El Arsenal naufraga en Brighton en el estreno goleador de Chema Andrés
articles.standfirst: Los de Arteta no recibían una goleada de tal calibre (3-0) desde mayo de 2023... ante el propio Brighton
articles.summary: Los de Arteta no recibían una goleada de tal calibre (3-0) desde mayo de 2023... ante el propio Brighton
articles.body: El Arsenal, ya con la tranquilidad que le otorgó el título de Premier cosechado el curso pasado, había firmado un inicio de temporada impecable con pleno de victorias en todas las competiciones. A su paso por el AMEX, sin embargo, recibieron su mayor goleada (3-0) desde mayo de 2023... a manos del propio Brighton. Chema Andrés, canterano del Real Madrid al que incorporaron este verano, puso la 'puntilla'. Después del carrusel de rotaciones introducido en Carabao, Arteta recuperó a sus hombres de confianza: Timber ya pudo arrancar de inicio, Konsa sigue cubriendo la lesión de Saliba y Bruno Guimaraes fue recompensado tras su gol ante el Sunderland. En el Brighton, Chema Andrés disfrutó de su primera titularidad en la sala de máquinas junto a un veterano como Gross. Se respiraba un ambiente especial en un AMEX que celebraba los 125 años de historia de su club. Los jugadores del Brighton no se quedaron atrás y sometieron a un alto grado de estrés al Arsenal. La presión alta fue asfixiante... y Raya tuvo que estirarse para evitar el tanto de Kostoulas cuando apenas habían transcurrido seis minutos. Se antojaba complicado sostener semejante nivel de intensidad y fue Odegaard quien levantó la mano para ordenar al Arsenal. Vino a recibir a zona de centrales y desplomó las revoluciones del encuentro. Sin embargo, justo cuando se cumplía la primera media hora de encuentro, Gross recibió en la frontal y, viendo que nadie le encimaba, sorprendió a Raya con un disparo al palo corto que entró tras tocar en la madera. Le hizo daño el gol a un Arsenal que no estaba encontrando la manera de asomarse por los dominios de Verbruggen. La tuvo Saka, forzado, cuando ya asomaba el descuento de la primera parte. Pero, a la contra, se encontraron con el 2-0 del Brighton. Esta vez, fue Kostoulas —asistente de Gross— quien recibió en la frontal, de nuevo retrocedió la zaga 'gunner' y conectó un 'zapatazo' ajustado al palo al que no llegó Raya. El Arsenal se había visto superado como hace tiempo que no sucedía. Arteta, sin embargo, optó por no realizar ningún ajuste para afrontar la segunda parte. El guion, sin embargo, no cambió: Kostoulas avisó con un disparo cruzado, Kadioglu reclamó un penalti y, a la salida de un córner, Chema Andrés les dio de su propia medicina. Primer gol en Inglaterra para el 'mini Rodri' formado en La Fábrica. Fue entonces cuando Arteta metió en el campo al mismo tiempo a Merino y un Zubimendi que, aunque alternó con Rice, volvió a ubicarse por momento como lateral derecho. Tampoco tardaron en entrar Eze y Gyökeres... y acabó 'quemando naves' dándole la alternativa a un Max Dowman que venía de marcar un doblete en Carabao. No era la tarde del Arsenal y, definitivamente, quedó confirmado con el mano a mano que Verbruggen le sacó a Havertz con el pie en el 77' para evitar que se reenganchasen al partido. Raya, incluso, evitó el cuarto. No debería generar dudas este 'borrón'. Pero se marchan al primer parón de la temporada dejando un mal sabor de boca... y abriendo la puerta a que el Manchester City se coloque como líder en solitario.

articles.title: Wisconsin's 3 'Badger Bakers' Concession Menu Items Displayed in New Close-Up Photo
articles.summary: Wisconsin is introducing a trio of baked potatoes to concession stand menus for the 2026 college football season.
articles.body:
Wisconsin is introducing a trio of baked potatoes to concession stand menus for the 2026 college football season.

Front Office Sports' Stadium Eats shared a photo Saturday of three potatoes being sold as "badger bakers" at Camp Randall Stadium.

Options include a "poutine baker" topped with smoked brisket, gravy and cheese curds and a "sweet corn baker" filled with buttered corn.

The "classic baker" features cheddar cheese, bacon bits and sour cream.

After opening their home slate with last Saturday's win over non-major Western Illinois, the Badgers are back in Madison for a Saturday matchup against Eastern Michigan.

articles.title: El Sporting gana por primera vez en El Principado y hace pleno fuera de El Molinón
articles.standfirst: El Andorra no sacó provecho de su dominio y enlaza su quinta derrota seguida
articles.summary: El Andorra no sacó provecho de su dominio y enlaza su quinta derrota seguida
articles.body: El Andorra, que empezaba ya el sábado en descenso tras el triunfo del Córdoba, no ha podido levantar cabeza ante el Sporting y ha encadenado su quinta derrota consecutiva. Si bien ha sido capaz de reaccionar al tanto rival inicial gijonés, volvió a echar en falta el peligro en los metros finales. El equipo asturiano, por su parte, ha vuelto a la senda del triunfo y se mete momentáneamente en 'playoffs'. Además consigue el primer triunfo de su historia en El Principado y hace pleno en los partidos fuera de El Molinón. Después de dos primeros avisos de los andorranos, los visitantes han abierto rápido la lata a la salida de un córner que, lanzado por Álex Corredera, Aimar Duñabeitia ha rematado con la testa luego de superar a su par. Como manda su estilo, los pupilos de Gerard Piqué han continuado con el balón, aunque eso no ha comportado tener la iniciativa. Al menos, al inicio, pues a partir del ecuador del primer tiempo los pirenaicos han metido una marcha más. Con un buen puñado de minutos muy lentos, tampoco se ha visto ninguna acción de peligro y así se han ido a la media parte. A la vuelta, el cambio le ha salido perfecto a Carles Manso, pues Jordi Cano ha empatado el duelo con el primer balón que ha tocado luego de aprovechar un error de Pablo Vázquez. Con los rojiblancos aturdidos y los locales cómodos, Cano ha vuelto a probar para encontrarse esta vez con Rubén Yáñez, igual que luego con Nacho Quintana. Todas las ocasiones que han faltado en la primera parte han llegado en la segunda, y ha sido también con turno para el Sporting, con Guille Rosas y un zurdazo al que Jesús Owono ha sacado una gran mano para que el tiro terminase en el travesaño. Justo en la siguiente, el 1-2, con tanto de Antonio Casas tras una buena individualidad de Juan Otero. Con el partido resuelto y el Andorra entregado al ataque, también con el guardameta ecuatoguineano, Nikita Iosifov ha culminado un contraataque a portería vacía.

articles.title: Sivera reina en San Mamés
articles.standfirst: El portero del Alavés para un penalti a Sancet y sostiene el trabajo de su equipo
articles.summary: El portero del Alavés para un penalti a Sancet y sostiene el trabajo de su equipo
articles.body: En este tipo de partidos hay que ponerse en la piel del sufridor de San Mamés en la Tribuna Este -con el sol cayendo a plomo- o de aquel que ha dejado compromisos familiares por acudir a ver su equipo. Y, claro, más todavía de aquellos que, sean de Athletic o Alavés, han acompañado el encuentro con un largo desplazamiento. No menos de cientos de ellos aborrecerían el momento en el que decidieron que el derbi merecía la pena. Sobre todo en la trinchera que se convirtió el encuentro en el primer periodo. ¡Qué tortura! El Alavés se manejó a distancia de Simón. Tanto que cualquiera diría que ésta se levantaba en la explanada más próxima al puerto de Algeciras. Llegar al dominio rojiblanco costó un mundo a los de Quique. Pero el Athletic no tuvo tampoco mucho de lo que presumir. Estuvo mucho más tiempo que su rival en campo ajeno aunque lo hizo sin fluidez en la circulación, sin frescura en el movimiento y con la misma efervescencia que un zumo de arándanos. Hubo disparos, sí, pero casi todos ellos entre desmembrados y de corcho. Sivera intervino sin demasiados alardes a los intentos de Jauregizar y Robert Navarro mientras que siguió con la mirada los desviados remates de Yuri y Johaneko. La segunda mitad iba por el mismo camino de aparente comodidad para el Alavés y desasosiego del Athletic cuando a Terzic le dio por intervenir. Metió a Berenguer y Maroan a la vez que retrasaba a Sancet al centro del campo. La respuesta fue una avalancha de cinco minutos con muy buena presencia en el área y una intervención de Sivera a lanzamiento de Yuri. Los que habían dado la tarde por perdida regresaron a la vida. Quique también actuó apostando por Toni Martínez en el lugar de Mariano. El técnico del Alavés equilibró de nuevo las piezas del tablero y lo empezó a decantar hacia su lado. Bordeando el minuto 70 el árbitro pitó penalti de Tenaglia sobre Nico y San Mamés creyó haber estado en las puertas de la victoria. No fue así porque Sivera estuvo más fino que el lanzador Sancet. Tocó entonces que los técnicos volvieran a retocar para que el partido no se fuera de los carriles ideados. En esas le fue mejor al Alavés, que apaciguó la sexta marcha del Athletic al tiempo que hizo por aparecer en campo contrario, donde Toni Martínez tuvo una gran opción cuando el reloj amenazaba el final.

articles.title: West Ham United: Taty Castellanos accused of spitting at Millwall's Filip Marschall
articles.summary: Millwall keeper Filip Marshcall alleges he was spat at by West Ham forward Taty Castellanos during their 2-2 draw.
articles.body:
On a day when eyes were focused on The Den with a fear that a fierce football rivalry could see the supporters of Millwall and West Ham make the headlines, it was one of the players that sparked the controversy.

Taty Castellanos is at the centre of the storm, after it was alleged the 27-year-old West Ham forward spat at Millwall keeper Filip Marschall during a pulsating game which ended in a 2-2 draw and with the Hammers down to 10 men.

The controversy, which unfortunately took some of the shine off an incredible contest, occurred in the 65th minute with the Lions leading 2-0.

Marschall was waiting with the ball at his feet until he was closed down, only picking it up to launch a clearance as Castellanos raced forward to apply pressure.

TV cameras caught Marschall, 23, appearing to show Premier League referee Paul Tierney a spot on his shirt he claimed was spit.

After the game, broadcasters were told Millwall had lodged a complaint to the match officials.

Millwall boss Alex Neil and Hammers counterpart Nuno Espirito Santo both told reporters they had not seen the incident, which was on the far side of the pitch from the dugouts.

Neil said: "I haven't asked [Filip] about it, but it's like anything else. I'm sure there'll be footage of it - or not if it didn't happen.

"I'd be extremely surprised if Filip's made an accusation and nothing's happened. I'm sure the authorities will deal with it.

"I didn't know what had happened, I'd just seen Filip walking out with the ball and thinking 'Where's he going?'.

"And then the fourth official basically said that there was an accusation of spitting."

Nuno added: "I'm aware of the allegation. I didn't see the images, I didn't speak with Taty [Castellanos].

"I cannot go much further on that, I'm sorry. For me to answer that, I have to see it. I'm going to look at the images. I cannot answer."

Spitting offences typically come with a six-match ban, if proven.

West Ham come from two goals down to secure derby draw at Millwall

Neil: 'Best atmosphere I've seen at the Den!'

'We are learning, but we can't waste time'

The incident was a blot on a positive second half from the Hammers, who changed shape and intensity to wipe out a two-goal deficit.

Nuno told BBC Radio London: "It was a tough, tough game. We didn't start very well, it was a very intense atmosphere and we didn't deal with the physicality.

"The second half we improved in our game. Our passing was better. The players showed up - I'm happy for that but I'm disappointed we didn't stick to the plan.

"In the end our fans were happy, not in the way they wanted. But the way the game went I think it's a positive result."

The Portuguese said the three-week international break comes at a good time for the Hammers, who can work on the defensive fragility which led to both Millwall goals.

"We are learning [about this division] but we can't waste much time," he added. "We are being punished with the physicality.

"Just look at the goals we are conceding from throw-ins, it's worrying. This international break will be very useful for us."

articles.title: Nick Saban Hypes Chambliss as 'Most Dynamic Player,' Lacy as Best RB While Picking LSU vs. Ole Miss
articles.summary: Former Alabama head football coach Nick Saban heaped praise on Ole Miss prior to its massive home game against LSU on Saturday night.
articles.body:
Former Alabama head football coach Nick Saban heaped praise on Ole Miss prior to its massive home game against LSU on Saturday night.

Saban paid significant compliments to Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss and running back Kewan Lacy, but still picked LSU to win, much to the dismay of guest picker Morgan Freeman on ESPN College GameDay .

"I think Trinidad Chambliss is the most dynamic player in college football," Saban said. "I think [Kewan Lacy] is the best running back in football. I love Pete Golding as a defensive coach, and I think he'll have them ready, but defense travels and LSU has the better defense, so I'm taking LSU."

While best known for coaching at Alabama for 17 seasons and winning six national championships, Saban was the head coach at LSU for five seasons before that and led the Tigers to the national title in 2003.

In addition to coaching at LSU, Saban worked extensively with current LSU head coach Lane Kiffin.

From 2014 to 2016, Kiffin was Saban's offensive coordinator at Alabama, and during that time the Crimson Tide went a combined 40-4.

Kiffin brought Chambliss and Lacy to Ole Miss, but when he took the LSU head coaching job at the end of the 2025 regular season, the Rebels decided to move on without him.

Defensive coordinator Pete Golding was promoted from defensive coordinator to head coach prior to the College Football Playoff, and he led the Rebels to the CFP semifinals.

Although Kiffin succeeded in bringing multiple players and coaches with him from Ole Miss to LSU, the Rebels managed to retain their two biggest stars in Chambliss and Lacy.

After starring at Division II Ferris State, Chambliss was a revelation at Ole Miss last season, completing 66.1 percent of his passes for 3,937 yards, 22 touchdowns and three interceptions to go along with 527 yards and eight scores on the ground.

Meanwhile, Lacy rushed for 1,567 yards and 24 touchdowns, the latter of which ranked him second among all FBS players and first among players in Power Four conferences.

Saturday night could be a challenge for Chambliss, Lacy and the Ole Miss offense and Kiffin and many of the LSU assistants are familiar with the type of offense they run.

At the same time, Golding is a defensive guru who is well aware of what Kiffin typically loves to do on offense as well.

No. 8 Ole Miss vs. No. 7 LSU figures to be a chess match, and it is fair to wonder if the advantage will ultimately rest with the Rebels due to the presence of elite offensive talents like Chambliss and Lacy.

articles.title: Jeremiah Smith Makes Ohio State History as Heisman Trophy Hype Continues to Stir
articles.summary: Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has officially cemented himself atop the Buckeyes' all-time receiving list.
articles.body:
Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has officially cemented himself atop the Buckeyes' all-time receiving list.

With a 23-yard catch in the first quarter Saturday against Kent State, Smith set Ohio State's new all-time receiving record, surpassing Michael Jenkins' previous mark of 2,898 yards.

One of a handful of top Heisman Trophy contenders, Smith entered Saturday's game second behind Miami quarterback Darian Mensah with +750 odds to take home college football's most prestigious hardware, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

Smith has been the centerpiece of Ohio State's passing attack throughout his tenure at the school.

During his freshman season in 2024, he caught 76 passes for 1,315 yards and 15 touchdowns while helping the Buckeyes capture a national championship.

Last year, Smith led the Big Ten with 87 receptions and 1,243 yards. He also found the end zone 12 times.

Smith's 2,558 receiving yards and 27 touchdown grabs from 2024 to 2025 were the most by any Big Ten receiver throughout their first two years in college.

He still hasn't shown any signs of slowing down to open the 2026 season.

articles.title: Johaneko es el chico para todo
articles.standfirst: Terzic sorprende esta vez colocando al vascofrancés de inicio en el lateral derecho
articles.summary: Terzic sorprende esta vez colocando al vascofrancés de inicio en el lateral derecho
articles.body: El lateral derecho en el inicio del partido ante el Alavés fue para Johaneko, futbolista que ha entrado como un rayo en el primer equipo y se ha convertido en el chico para todo de Terzic. Arrancó el curso como alternativa a Yuri en el lateral izquierdo y después de haber jugado en ese mismo costado más adelantado ahora aparece como lateral derecho. No fue su mejor día. Tampoco el de muchos de sus compañeros. El cambio no es circunstancial porque también lo quiso poner ahí en el partido suspendido ante el Levante. La apuesta de Terzic tiene su punto de riesgo por la carga de exigencia que ofrece tanto baile en la posición con la necesidad de rendir al máximo nivel. El caso es que Johaneko (22 años) ha escalado hasta la titularidad en un perfil que en teoría deberían repartirse entre Areso y Rincón porque su sitio inicial estaba en el otro lado. Ahí competiría con Yuri ya que Adama, que en agosto fue aspirante al lateral izquierdo, salió cedido al West Ham el último día de mercado. Este septiembre no ha sido amable con Adama, que tiene contrato en Bilbao hasta 2029, porque tampoco termina de volar en Londres: 13 minutos jugados con el West Ham y 20 con el Athletic. Ha intervenido en un partido con cada equipo. Lo que dejó claro el derbi con el Alavés es que la asistencia volvió a bajar con respecto a las jornadas precedentes. Hay una pérdida continuada de aficionados en los cuatro partidos que se han disputado esta temporada. El estreno frente al Sevilla reunió a 49.416 espectadores y el partido de este sábado con el Alavés quedó en 47.254. Los hinchas han ido cayendo a medida que se van sumando las jornadas.

articles.title: Zion Suzuki: Japan goalkeeper lays platform for Aston Villa's victory at Spurs
articles.summary: Aston Villa new boy Zion Suzuki deserves as much credit as anyone for their first Premier League win of the season at struggling Tottenham.
articles.body:
While Johan Manzambi and Nicolas Jackson both scored, another Aston Villa new boy, Zion Suzuki, deserved as much credit as anyone for their first Premier League win of the season at struggling Tottenham.

The Japan goalkeeper made the move to Villa from Italian side Parma for a fee in the region of £30m in August.

And his performance against Spurs suggests he is more than capable of filling the very big boots vacated by the departure of Argentina number one - and fan favourite - Emiliano Martinez to Chelsea .

In particular, his two saves from Savio within seconds of each other and a moment of good fortune when Archie Gray's effort clipped wide off his foot, gave Villa the platform to ride out a period in the game when the hosts held sway.

"We needed the keeper," said Villa boss Unai Emery in his post-match interviews.

"He is a keeper to save us. To make sure in the goal he has the quality and then he has the skills to play and build up.

"It is very important how he is doing it and sometimes taking some risks, but through those he is improving and learning."

One of the attractions around signing the 24-year-old in August was his apparent assuredness with the ball at his feet and his ability to spray the ball forward with very little backlift.

And on a day when things could not have gone much better for him, Suzuki ended up as the architect of Villa's second goal, with his booming ball forward from his own six-yard box dropping deep into Tottenham territory, where Jackson collected it and dispatched an unerring shot to the left corner.

"In the build up, he can choose to play long balls because he has a very long pass in behind and he did that for the second goal we scored," added Emery.

Villa survive late Spurs fightback to earn first Premier League win

No revival in sight for 'fragile' Spurs after Villa defeat

Born in the United States to a Ghanaian father and a Japanese mother, Suzuki has already played in Japan, Belgium and Italy and won 28 caps for his country.

And speaking to BBC Sport in August, Dennis Rudel - his former coach at Sint-Truiden - stressed that Suzuki has the attributes to become one of the world's best in his position.

"It is possible if he stays healthy," said the former Union Berlin coach. "With his physical strength, there is no-one better in the world in terms of dynamic, jumping power, throws and kicking the ball.

"When I watched him at the World Cup [for Japan], his biggest strength was his mental clearness. His focus on the game or in training sessions is so good. He is always prepared and really disciplined.

"He is aiming to show he can be one of the best. He was immediately one of the top four or five goalkeepers in Serie A.

"As a person and as a player, he is a role model for how you should behave. I don't see any weakness in him."

"He has such big hands and he is powerful. When he can reach the ball, it is a 90-95% chance of a save. It is something really special."

articles.title: Northampton 1-0 Rotherham
articles.summary: Paul Mullin’s second-half penalty was enough for Rotherham to beat Northampton 1-0 at Sixfields.
articles.body:
A tight game was decided by Mullin's emphatic spot-kick 17 minutes from the end as the Millers won on the road for the first time this season.

Home goalkeeper Zach Jeacock clawed away Fabio Tavares' curling effort in the opening 10 minutes, but Northampton were the better side in the first half and had the majority of the play.

An excellent last-ditch tackle snuffed out Nathan Opoku when he found space in the box before Owen Dale shot over and Max Dyche headed straight at Julian Eyestone.

Rotherham almost snuck ahead right on half-time after Jeacock reacted smartly to deny Josh Austerfield, and Northampton's goalkeeper also kept out Mullin on the restart.

The visitors were in the ascendency for most of the second half and they made the crucial breakthrough when Mullin smashed home from the penalty spot after he was brought down by Dyche.

Northampton pushed for an equaliser but Harvey Saunders missed their big chance when thwarted by Eyestone in added time.

articles.title: Crewe 1-1 Shrewsbury
articles.summary: Shrewsbury earned a first away point of the season thanks to an opportunist goal from George Lloyd in a 1-1 draw at local rivals Crewe.
articles.body:
Jordan Gibson's far-post header had the Railwaymen in front midway through the first half, but the Shrews were back on level terms when Lloyd brushed past home goalkeeper Tom Booth to fire in before the interval.

Luca Hoole offered the first threat of the game for Shrewsbury when he cut in on the right of the box and drove an effort into the side-netting.

Gavin Cowan's side were the more enterprising side in the opening half but fell behind in the 24th minute after a neat interchange between Jack Lankester and the lively Joel Tabiner.

The latter was set free and he lofted a pinpoint cross over the face of goal for Gibson to head home.

The visitors were level in the 39th minute when Lloyd reacted quickest as Booth came out to collect Lewis Billington's under-hit headed backpass, nipping in to fire into an empty net.

Shrewsbury maintained their momentum after the break, although Isaac Lee sent a free header straight at Booth.

At the other end, Will Brook punched away a thumping free-kick from Gibson.

Shrews threatened in the closing minutes as Hoole sent a header against a post from a long free-kick.

Substitute Calum Agius thought he had grabbed a stoppage-time winner for Crewe, with the striker firing in off a post only for his effort to be ruled out for offside.

articles.title: Brighton 3-0 Arsenal: Mikel Arteta's side lose for first time this season as impressive hosts thrash defending champions
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Brighton thumped Arsenal 3-0 in a scoreline that flattered the Gunners; Pascal Gross and Charalampos Kostoulas put Brighton 2-0 up at half-time, Chema Andres made it three nine minutes after the break; Arsenal suffer first dropped points of season
articles.body:
The Gunners were chasing an eighth straight victory to start their season - and their best start to any campaign in 123 years - but were given a lesson in commitment and quality from the first minute from Fabian Hurzeler's team.

As Brighton pressed Arsenal into submission, long-range strikes from Pascal Gross and Charalampos Kostoulas put the Seagulls 2-0 up at half-time. Both Brighton players could not believe their luck at how much space they had.

Latest news and rumours: Brighton | Arsenal

The second strike from Kostoulas was a real sucker punch as it came 15 seconds after Bukayo Saka saw a close-range effort for an equaliser well-saved by Bart Verbruggen. It also showed how Arsenal took 44 minutes to have a meaningful chance.

And it got even better for Brighton nine minutes after half-time. Chema Andres got his first Brighton goal as he headed in Gross' corner at the far post, amid poor Arsenal marking.

Brighton could have added to their lead as Arsenal could not get out of their own half to fashion anything. Pascal Struijk nearly got a fourth but headed wide from a corner that David Raya came and failed to get. Then Matt O'Riley saw a one-on-one saved by Raya before Malick Yalcouye hit the woodwork at the rebound.

The result sees brilliant Brighton move up to third in the table, two points behind Arsenal. Meanwhile, Manchester City can go into the lengthy international break three points clear at the top of the Premier League with a win over Sunderland on Super Sunday, live on Sky Sports .

6: BIG SAVE! Arsenal are under the cosh straight away as Kostoulas' deflected shot is tipped behind by Raya.

30: GOAL! Brighton deservedly lead as Gross curls in a stunning effort from distance off Raya's near post.

39: CHANCE! Brighton continue their dominance as Yasin Ayari blasts into the side-netting after being teed up by Ferdi Kadioglu.

44: BIG ARSENAL CHANCE! Arsenal break in huge numbers and Martin Odegaard's effort is deflected into Saka's path, but his close-range effort is saved by Verbruggen.

45: GOAL! Fifteen seconds later, Brighton double their lead as Kostoulas' long-range drive finds the bottom corner.

52: RED CARD? On a booking, Kadioglu goes down under Riccardo Calafiori's challenge in the box, but is not booked a second time for simulation. No dive is given.

56: GOAL! Arsenal's task becomes even greater as Andres nods home from Gross' corner.

68: SO CLOSE! As Arsenal struggle to get out, Brighton nearly get a fourth as Raya fails to come for a corner and Struijk heads wide.

77: GOOD SAVE! Kai Havertz breaks clear for a huge chance on goal but Verbruggen makes the save.

80: WIDE! Substitute Georginio Rutter fires wide at the far post after a shot is played into his path.

89: BIG SAVE AND BAR! How have Brighton not added another? O'Riley runs through on goal but Raya saves, then Yalcouye strikes the bar from a tight angle at the rebound.

"A very disappointing result and performance. Full credit to Brighton in the manner they performed and went about the game. They were another gear from us in the basics of the game. They were always first in the first duel, in the second actions, second balls, and they started to play from there.

"And on top of that, when we had the ball, especially in our own half, we were extremely poor technically, not respecting the game and the game principles you have to apply against a team that want to press you man to man.

"That never gives you the option to dominate and control the game in the manner you want. And then when we had big chances, we didn't put them away.

"We have to make sure we learn the lesson because this can't happen again."

Hurzeler: We were horrible to play against

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler to Sky Sports:

"Beating the current champions and the best team in England is something special. But it's not because the result is special, it's the performance. The boys showed real togetherness and intensity.

"They were horrible to play against today and that's because we did the basic things right. Overall I was very pleased with the performance.

"I think we deserved to win. It's a moment the players and the staff can enjoy because they worked hard for this but it's also important why we had this success today, because we did the basics right and we were brilliant in the duels."

"Arsenal struggled badly. Brighton really closed them down and went after them. They wouldn't let them play out and they won the ball back consistently. They broke the press probably twice all day, Arsenal.

"The first goal put more air in Brighton's lungs and they just kept going and going. They thoroughly deserved it.

"We've got to give credit where credit's due. Arsenal weren't great but Brighton made them not look great. They were outstanding.

"You thought Arsenal would come out second half and have a go, they didn't. Chema and Kostoulas were outstanding. Kostoulas caused Konsa and Gabriel nightmares."

articles.summary: Andreas Weimann’s late penalty extended Cheltenham Town’s unbeaten run to five matches following a 1-1 draw at Colchester United.
articles.body:
Colchester had a third-minute penalty appeal rejected when Harry Anderson tumbled under Jake Evans' challenge just inside the area.

But Cheltenham almost went ahead just before the break when Colchester goalkeeper Thimothee Lo-Tutala saved Charlie McCann's close-range effort with his legs, after the ball had been headed across the area.

Colchester's Jack Payne was denied from close range by Cheltenham goalkeeper Wyll Stanway early in the second half.

But Colchester finally broke the deadlock in the 67th minute through Moses Sesay, who stroked a low shot into the net after breaking from midfield and exchanging passes with Ellis Iandolo.

However, Cheltenham equalised in the 78th minute when Weimann slotted home from the spot after Sean Raggett had handled Joe Tomlinson's free-kick in the area.

Colchester were reduced to 10 men in the 83rd when substitute Jaden Williams was sent off for a foul on Robbie Cundy, as the points were shared.

articles.title: Jeremiah Smith passes Michael Jenkins as Ohio State's all-time receiving yards leader
articles.summary: Saturday's game against Kent State was just the 32nd of Smith's career.
articles.body:
It took just 32 games for Jeremiah Smith to become Ohio State's all-time leading receiver.

The star junior receiver broke Michael Jenkins' school record for receiving yards early in the No. 6 Buckeyes' game against Kent State. Smith entered the game with 179 catches for 2,873 yards and trailed Jenkins by just 25 yards.

He set the record on his second catch of the game.

Jenkins played three seasons at Ohio State, but it took him nine more games than Smith to accrue his total. The first-round pick in the 2004 NFL Draft played for the Buckeyes from 2001-03.

Smith, meanwhile, can already claim to being the best wide receiver in Ohio State history just barely into his third season. Smith had 76 catches for 1,315 yards and 15 scores as a true freshman in 2024 as Ohio State bounced back from a loss to Michigan at the end of the regular season to win the College Football Playoff. A season ago, he played in three fewer games but had 87 catches for 1,243 yards and 12 scores.

Through the first two games of 2026, Smith had 16 catches for 315 yards and three scores. Smith had eight grabs for 164 yards and a TD in Ohio State's 24-23 loss to Texas in Week 2 and, along with Malachi Toney, is one of the few non-quarterback favorites to win the Heisman in December.

articles.title: Terzic: "La primera mitad ha sido la peor actuación de esta temporada"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador se confiesa enfadado con la respuesta del equipo y anuncia más trabajo
articles.summary: El entrenador se confiesa enfadado con la respuesta del equipo y anuncia más trabajo
articles.body: El empate con el Alavés fue un varapalo para las necesidades del Athletic. "Hay que separar las dos partes de este encuentro. La primera parte ha sido la peor actuación de nuestra temporada, imprecisos y sin claras oprotunidades. Queremos ser un equipo completo. Ha habido 24 tiros a puerta, pero no han sido del nivel que hacemos en el campo de entrenamiento. Estoy un poco decepcionado con lo que hemos mostrado en el campo. Esperamos más del equipo y de nosotros mismos", explicó Terzic. Los errores del equipo: "Todas las respuestas están en Lezama y ahí tenemos que utilizar el campo de entrenamiento para mejorar. No es cuestión de tener una reunión. Hay que trabajar bien y lo vamos a hacer. En la segunda mitad ha habido una mejora en la manera de controlar el juego y una buena defensa. Debemos ser más clínicos en el último tercio. A nivel individual todo el mundo tiene que dar un paso adelante. Estamos preparados, aunque pueda llevarnos algo de tiempo ser más constantes.No queremos ser un equipo que dependa de un momento clave como un penalti, queremos lograrlo de más maneras". 8 puntos sobre 18 posibles: "Que me sienta enfadado y decepcionado es posible. Son sensaciones que están bien para hoy, pero no para mañana. Nos vamos a levantar y preparar todo en los entrenamientos de la mejor manera posible en este tiempo que tenemos ahora sin Liga. Debemos tener más ocupación en el área del rival y estamos trabajando muy duro en todo esto. Hay frustración en todos nosotros y eso es bueno. Es algo que tenemos que cambiar en el campo de entrenamiento. Creo mucho en este grupo de jugadores y estoy convencido de que vamos a conseguir victorias rápidas. Cuatro partidos sin una derrota en la Liga no es malo, pero vamos a intentar también ganar". Las parejas de centrocampistas: "Cada jugador tiene sus características y en esa zona del campo intentamos mezclar jugadores con jugadores de más calidad con el balón y otros de más velocidad y presencia física". La entrada de Nico Serrano: "No hay ningún jugador en la plantilla que no me convenza. Quería un jugador con zurda por el lado derecho. Es un futbolista que ha trabajado durísimo en las últimas semanas. Confiamos en toda la plantilla". Enfrentarse a un rival cerrado: "Hablamos de Elche o Alavés y solo decís que defienden. El Elche fue uno de los que mayor posesión tuvo en las primeras jornadas y nosotros aquí les hicimos defender. La razón de nuestro juego es por lo que Elche o Alavés tienen que defender. Debemos mejorar nuestro comportamiento". El lanzador de penaltis: "Nosotros decidimos porque también es una cuestión que entrenamos. El de este sábado es el primer penalti que le he visto fallar. Vamos a tratar de asegurarnos de que el siguiente lo marque".

articles.title: Arteta pulls no punches after Arsenal shambles at Brighton
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta delivered a stark assessment after Arsenal’s nine-match Premier League winning run ended with a 3-0 defeat at Brighton.Photo by Clive Rose/Getty...
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta delivered a stark assessment after Arsenal 's nine-match Premier League winning run ended with a 3-0 defeat at Brighton .

Arsenal delivered a disaster performance at Brighton , losing 3-0 at the Amex as their nine-match Premier League winning run came to an abrupt end at the Ammex.

Two long-range goals, poor defending from a corner and a blunt attacking display combined to punish a side who never found their usual rhythm.

The stats may suggest a more even contest than the scoreline, but Arsenal never looked in control and capable of taking anything from this game.

Mikel Arteta made no attempt to disguise his frustration afterwards.

"Extremely disappointed," said Arteta after the match .

"But first of all, I think we have to congratulate Brighton for the victory. I think they deserve it. I think they were the better team. And from our side, there were certain basics that you need to accomplish in football, especially in the Premier League, that we were very far from.

"[We didn't] win the first duel or every second ball. That put the game, especially how direct they were, in a really difficult place for us.

"On top of that, when we did regain the ball, especially in our half, the amount of technical errors that we did, we didn't respect any principle of play that you have to, to get out of that man-to-man situation, so that put us always in the back foot, so it was very difficult to control the game.

"When we had moments of dominance and control, then we opened them up, but we didn't as well finish those actions with the quality that is required to compensate all the other things that you have done. So at the end of the day, I think they deserve to win the game, and it's a big lesson for us.

"Well, the first one, it was Brighton; they were really good, and they had another bite, and their timing was better.

"There are a lot of moments when the ball is fifty-fifty, and it changes hands, and most of the time it was for them. Sometimes there were some technical errors very much involved that opened us up in a really difficult way, but that's something to learn.

"That's not going to take away what the team has done, and the boys have done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup.

"Because with 18 players coming back, what we've done and the way we've competed and the amount of games that we won has been remarkable, but this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level."

Arteta's assessment was difficult to dispute.

Arsenal were second best in the areas he identified, losing too many duels and second balls while repeatedly surrendering possession as Brighton pressed.

There were periods when the Gunners managed to push Brighton back and create openings, but they lacked the quality required to turn those moments into goals.

For Arsenal, the task now is to ensure a dreadful afternoon on the south coast remains exactly that, a single bad performance rather than the start of something more damaging.

articles.title: Brighton defeat a 'big lesson' against complacency for Arsenal, says Arteta
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta said Arsenal's 3-0 defeat by Brighton was a reminder of "how tough every game" in the Premier League is as the defending champions were beaten f...
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta said Arsenal 's 3-0 defeat by Brighton was a reminder of "how tough every game" in the Premier League is as the defending champions were beaten for the first time this season.

Brighton dominated from the off at the Amex Stadium and punched holes in Arsenal's normally resolute defence thanks to long-range strikes from Pascal Gross and Charalampos Kostoulas before half-time.

Chema Andres rose highest to head in a third from a corner early in the second period as Arsenal lost by more than two goals for the first time in over three years.

"Extremely disappointed. First of all I think we have to congratulate Brighton for the victory, I think they deserve it," said Arteta.

"I think they were the better team. From our side there were certain basics that you need to accomplish in football, especially in the Premier League, that we were very far from."

The Gunners have been tipped to cruise to the title after ending their 22-year wait to be crowned champions of England last season.

Arsenal started the campaign in ominous fashion, winning all seven games before Saturday in all competitions.

But Arteta said defeat served a timely reminder ahead of a three-week international break of how tough the season will be.

"It's a big lesson for us. Is that a reminder to some of the players how tough every game is," added the Spaniard.

"That's not going to take away what the team has done and the boys have done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup.

"With 18 players coming back, what we've done and the way we've competed and the amount of games we've won has been remarkable.

"But this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level."

articles.title: Laporta: "No hacemos política con el Barça, pero sí país"
articles.standfirst: El presidente del Barça responde a los socios en la Asamblea General de 2026 celebrada hoy
articles.summary: El presidente del Barça responde a los socios en la Asamblea General de 2026 celebrada hoy
articles.body: Joan Laporta respondió a algunas de las preguntas que hicieron los socios en la parte final de la Asamblea General de este sábado. El presidente del Barcelona defendió la catalanidad del club a la vez que se mostró satisfecho de apoyar a la selección española de fútbol y de querer hacer de la entidad una institución global y abierta. "Estamos muy orgullosos de nuestro catalanismo, es la Junta más catalanista de la historia. Defendemos nuestras libertades y tenemos claro nuestro compromiso, pero debemos ser una Junta de todos los culés y pensamientos, siempre que se respete la democracia. Es importante tener un Barça global, cuantos más globales, más fuertes y libres seremos. Espero que todos los culés estén cómodos. No hacemos política con el Barça, pero sí país", aseguró Laporta. El abogado también contestó a un socio que le criticó su apoyo al combinado de Luis De La Fuente en el pasado Mundial: "Había ocho jugadores del Barcelona en la selección. El Barça ganó el Mundial. Era importante que estuviera allí, como presidente del Barcelona. Debía estar. El trato de la selección fue exquisito, pero eso no me hace renunciar a mi forma de pensar. Hay que construir puentes con la Federación y LaLiga". Por otro lado, Laporta, quien mantuvo que sigue en pie hacerle un homenaje a Messi, también se pronunció sobre la crítica que el club no cuida lo suficiente las secciones: "Estamos orgullosos de todas, configuran el club polideportivo más grande del mundo e invertimos todo lo que podemos. Pero provocaban menos margen salarial. De todas formas, siempre intentamos mantener la competitividad de todas las secciones. Estamos contentos. Dedicamos grandes esfuerzos. Acumulan 50 Champions. Pero la mayoría de ingresos vienen del fútbol y con ellos pagamos las secciones, esto es así".

articles.title: Portsmouth 2-2 Blackburn: Colby Bishop earns a point for Pompey
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Portsmouth and Blackburn Rovers at Fratton Park on Saturday; Colby Bishop strikes to earn a point for Pompey in entertaining draw.
articles.body:
John Mousinho made three changes from Pompey's dour 0-0 draw at Charlton with Bishop among those making way.

Tony Mowbray was also forced into making a change from Blackburn's win against Millwall as Yuri Ribeiro missed out with a hamstring issue and Harry Pickering came in.

The visitors started the brighter and Sam Morsy fed the ball through to captain Todd Cantwell inside the box, forcing the game's first corner via a deflected shot aimed point-blank at Daniel Bielica.

It was Pompey though who opened the scoring when Zak Swanson volleyed home past Rovers keeper Balazs Toth after Tyrese Shade's cross from the left was only half-cleared by Sean McLoughlin.

That lead lasted just seven minutes until Oladapo Afolayan netted his third goal in two games by converting a right-footed strike into the near post, making the most of a chipped ball played to him from the centre of the field by Pickering.

Bielica was forced into action again to scramble away Afolayan's flick-on from close range and then straight down the other end, Ryan Kavuma-McQueen scuffed an effort high and wide after a well-worked move which began with the receiving of a 40-yard diagonal switch from Madiodio Dia.

Abu Kamara was denied a first goal back in Pompey colours when Pickering timed a sliding challenge inside the penalty area well to clear the danger as the winger was preparing to shoot.

Home captain Marlon Pack received the game's first yellow card following a tackle in midfield on Rovers goalscorer Afolayan five minutes before the interval.

After surviving 10 minutes of Pompey dominance in the opening stages of the second half, Rovers took the lead for the first time in the game through Ryoya Morishita's drilled effort into the far corner, set up by Afolayan.

Mousinho's misery with injuries was further compounded by the forced withdrawal of Conor Shaughnessy, who pulled up unchallenged and had to be replaced after an hour.

His side did however claw their way back into the game when substitute Bishop inadvertently deflected in Kavuma-McQueen's right-footed effort after the Chelsea loanee did superbly to keep the opportunity alive for the hosts

Pompey had chances to snatch a third through Kamara and Bishop but were unable to find that late winner as the points were shared.

Both Mousinho and Mowbray will be relatively satisfied to head into the first international break of the season with a draw.

articles.title: Birmingham 2-2 Middlesbrough: Adilson Malanda earns late point for Boro
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Birmingham City and Middlesbrough at St Andrew's on Saturday; Adilson Malanda earns late point for Boro after James Beadle error in entertaining draw.
articles.body:
The defender was on hand to punish Birmingham goalkeeper James Beadle's handling error when the home side seemingly had the game won after coming from a goal down.

Blues made a good start, creating a couple of chances to open the scoring.

The first came in the fourth minute when Jhon Solis dispossessed Malanda and was given the ball back by Tomoki Iwata. The Colombian turned and dragged his shot narrowly wide.

Fourteen minutes later the hosts went from one end of the field to the other, freeing Carlos Vicente down the right. The winger back-heeled to Bright Osayi-Samuel, who picked out Luis Vazquez. After last weekend's horror miss at Derby, the Argentine did at least put his header on target but too close to Radek Vitek who tipped over.

Boro grew into the game with Amario Cozier-Duberry causing Birmingham huge problems down the right.

The Brighton loanee should have scored nine minutes before the break when Myles Peart-Harris picked him out with a pull-back but he scooped his shot over the bar.

The 21-year-old's influence grew and it was no surprise when Malanda hit him with a sweeping, 45th-minute diagonal and he weaved his way into the area to set up Max Arfsten. The American fired first-time into the top corner.

Chris Davies' side responded well after the restart and levelled 10 minutes in when Malanda lost possession to Iwata who then invited Solis to surge into the area. Just as the midfielder looked to be running out of angle, Liam Millar popped up to fire home his first Blues goal.

Four minutes later the home side were in front when Millar's deep corner was headed back into the six-yard box by Jay Stansfield. The ball pinballed around and eventually went in off Riley McGree.

With 20 minutes to go Iwata went close when he popped up at the near post to glance a Millar cross just over the bar.

The visitors pressed and made attacking substitutions with Tommy Conway, Kyle Joseph and Jeremy Sarmiento and they did push Birmingham on to the defensive.

The pressure eventually paid off with two minutes to go when Sebastian Berhalter curled over an inswinging free-kick which seemed to run harmlessly through to Beadle.

However, the goalkeeper fumbled four yards out and, while Joseph was unable to bundle home, Malanda did to send the travelling supporters home happy.

articles.title: Wrexham 2-1 Southampton: Keven Schlotterbeck's late own goal seals win for Red Dragons
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Wrexham and Southampton at the Racecourse Ground on Saturday; Keven Sclotterbeck scores a late own goal to cost Saints in defeat.
articles.body:
Phil Parkinson's men headed into Saturday's clash reeling from a 6-0 hammering at West Ham and desperate to kickstart their campaign with a first home Championship win of the campaign.

Kieffer Moore headed Wrexham into the lead during an opening period the visitors dominated and James Ward-Prowse's first goal since his return to saw Southampton level shortly after the break.

Saints pushed after Daniel Peretz prevented Moore scoring an outrageous strike from the halfway line, but the Welsh side edged a late win as Schlotterbeck turned in Jacques Ekomie's cross.

"You only win when you're spying," bellowed triumphant Wrexham fans just days before Southampton boss Tonda Eckert faces a Football Association hearing over the 'Spygate' scandal.

Wrexham co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac made a light-hearted social media jibe about the saga in the lead-up a game their side started on the backfoot.

Finn Azaz all too easily forced an early save and the hosts found in-form Southampton striker Cyle Larin a handful.

The Canada international attempted an audacious attempt from just inside the hosts' half and lifted another effort over, having failed to convert a variety of crosses sent his way.

Wrexham were being outplayed, yet Southampton's inability to take their chances allowed Parkinson's side to land the first blow.

Callum O'Hare forced a great save from Peretz and Southampton were found wanting from the resulting corner. Ben Whiteman sent over the 35th-minute set-piece and towering Moore powered home a header.

Saints were unable to eke out an equaliser before the break, but levelled five minutes into the second half.

A driven James Bree cross deflected into the path of Ward-Prowse, who followed a blocked initial attempt with a thumping follow-up effort.

That hard work was so nearly undone in the 55th minute when Moore went agonisingly close to scoring the goal of his life.

Picking up an aimless Saints pass, the striker quickly took aim from just inside Southampton's half and saw his shot tipped over by backpedalling Peretz.

Wrexham were furious to see a goal-kick awarded and their mood would have darkened had Anthony Patterson not stopped Ward-Prowse whipping in a free-kick.

Ryan Manning volleyed over as Southampton pushed to take the lead, but Wrexham were keeping the visitors at arm's length.

Parkinson's men kept fighting and their endeavour was rewarded in the 89th minute.

Ekomie made space to send in a low cross from the left that Schlotterbeck turned into his own goal under pressure from O'Hare.

"It feels amazing. First of all, I'd like to thank our supporters. The way they got behind the team today was absolutely fantastic.

"The reception they gave me as I walked across the pitch before the game meant a lot.

"Our supporters have had tough times and they're used to bouncing back and they played their part today. I thought they were incredible and it was a proper atmosphere in the ground and that's what it's all about.

"The club, the supporters, the staff, the owners, the players - everybody's linked together and you could feel that today."

"I think that we controlled large parts of the game. I think there's more than enough moments to go up in the first half. We didn't manage to do that.

"I think even in the second half we knew that coming out of half-time we need to get a first one and then keep pushing and I think we've done that.

"Over 90 minutes today I think we talk about one corner and one flick after a long ball from the goalkeeper."

articles.title: Burnley 1-1 Derby: Clarets still winless after Rams level late on
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Burnley and Derby County at Turf Moor on Saturday; Mohammed Fuseini scores to deny Nicky Hayen a first league win as Clarets boss.
articles.body:
The Ghana winger, signed on loan from Belgian club Union Saint-Gilloise on transfer deadline day, drilled in an angled shot on the run, via the inside of the far post, for his first Derby goal.

Zeki Amdouni's 34th-minute far-post header looked to have given Burnley a much-needed victory to ease the pressure on their new head coach Nicky Hayen, already facing questions over his future despite only having taken charge in July.

Switzerland forward Amdouni bounced his far-post header into the net after goalkeeper Josh Vickers had flapped at a Lucas Pires corner.

But Fuseini's equaliser leaves Burnley winless and bottom of the Championship, having failed to gain three points from a match Hayen had described beforehand as "must-win".

Hayen had made six changes to try to revive a team beaten at Swansea last weekend - dropping goalkeeper Max Weiss and former Manchester City defender Kyle Walker, and bringing back winger Marcus Edwards, re-registered after being left out of Burnley's 25-man EFL squad at the start of the month.

Derby, themselves in the bottom three and with a long injury list, created the first two chances just after the quarter-hour mark. Midfielder David Ozoh's shot from outside the penalty area was deflected wide, and from the resulting corner delivered by Joe Ward, defender Dion Sanderson met the ball at the far post but could only head the ball back across goal.

Amdouni then headed Burnley in front with the game's first effort on target, but Derby could have drawn level three minutes before half-time. Former Blackburn forward Sammie Szmodics ran clear on to a long pass from Ward but was stopped as he collided with Gregoire Coudert.

With the goalkeeper down, Ryan Hedges' follow-up was blocked by Igor Julio, before Carlton Morris played the loose ball wide to Szmodics, whose shot from a tight angle was cleared from inside the six-yard box by Anel Ahmedhodzic.

Ozoh threatened an equaliser 50 seconds after half-time with a run down the left, which ended with a fierce angled shot that Coudert beat away at his near post, and Hedges then drove a good chance wide from 12 yards as Burnley failed to deal with a long throw.

Burnley, having ridden those scares, began to create pressure as they sought a second goal, and substitute Largie Ramazani was only denied by a fine Sanderson block after Jacob Bruun Larsen had exchanged passes with Pires to set him up.

Coudert made an excellent save low to his left to push away Bobby Clark's 20-yard drive inside the final quarter of an hour, but Derby drew level when Rhian Brewster sent fellow substitute Fuseini away to equalise.

articles.title: Newcastle 2-1 Hull City: Joe Willock and Lewis Hall on target as Magpies edge Premier League thriller at St James' Park
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Newcastle claim a 2-1 victory against Hull  at St. James Park; Joe Willock and Lewis Hall netted inside the first 10 minutes; Mohamed-Ali Cho's second-half strike was not enough to restore parity for the Tigers
articles.body:
Harvey Barnes' neat through-ball allowed Willock to smash past Konstantinos Tzolakis inside three minutes, and the inspired Barnes was rewarded with his second assist of the game when left-back Hall fired home a pinpoint finish into the bottom-left corner just four minutes later to put Newcastle firmly in control.

The first half ended on a sour note for the home side, though, as Yoane Wissa missed the chance to put his side three up on the stroke of half-time. His penalty was expertly saved by Tzolakis after Sorba Thomas - making his first league start - was deemed to have fouled Jacob Murphy, bringing down the winger with an outstretched arm.

Latest news and rumours: Newcastle | Hull

It was a miss that was ever so close to proving costly, as a resilient Hull came into the second half buoyed, and their spell of dominance was rewarded when substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho's finish kissed the post and nestled in the Newcastle net just after the hour mark.

Hull ramped up the pressure for the final 15 minutes, with full-backs Lewie Coyle and Ryan Giles whipping in cross after cross.

The best chance fell to summer signing Tim Iroegbunam, whose close-range volley was inches away from finding the top-right corner, but a determined Newcastle held on to secure a much-needed three points after their 4-1 drubbing at Leeds on Monday, thereby ending Hull's fairytale beginning to Premier League life.

3: GOAL! Lovely work from Barnes allows Willock to smash past Tzolakis from just inside the box to put Newcastle in front from their first meaningful attack of the game

7: GOAL! Hall makes it two with a pinpoint finish into the bottom-left corner after another brilliant run and throughball from Barnes - his second assist in the first 10 minutes!

15: CAREFUL! Lukas Hornicek almost hands Hull a goal as Mohamed Belloumi robs him of the ball on the six-yard line, but the goalkeeper smothers at the second attempt and the ball is cleared!

22: CHANCE! Matt Crooks' bending low cross almost finds Thomas in the box but Sean Steur is there to clear his lines expertly!

32: SO CLOSE! A brilliant fizzed cross from Murphy is somehow missed by both Wissa and Barnes, and Hall's eventual back-post effort is spooned over!

45: PENALTY SAVED! Wissa cannot convert from the spot! Thomas is adjudged to have fouled Murphy with an outstretched hand brushing the winger's leg, but Tzolakis gets down ever so well to tip it round the right-hand post!

67: GOAL! Cho gets one back for Hull just four minutes after coming on with an expert finish that kisses the post and nestles in the net!

81: SO, SO CLOSE! It looks for all the world that Iroegbunam has equalised, but his close-range volley is inches above the crossbar and Newcastle hold on!

Newcastle head coach Matthias Jaissle, speaking to Sky Sports:

"It was a tough match. We wanted to show a reaction after Leeds and we did it at a really high level in the first half - it was probably the best one so far in the season.

"We could have killed the game, actually, if we scored a third goal - I think that would have been much, much easier than in the second half.

"We need to be honest - there were many changes along the way. We have nine players injured - that didn't help in the second half when Hull was bringing everything in our box, but I'm so proud.

"Big, big, big, respect, and we are so happy to take the three points."

Jakirovic: We lost this game in the first half

Hull head coach Sergej Jakirovic, speaking to Sky Sports:

"I'm very proud. Especially second half, I think we were the better team. We pressed a lot, we pushed a lot.

"We had our opportunities there and we couldn't use them, and we have to congratulate Newcastle. They won this game in the first half - we were poor.

"We should be better, especially in the beginning - we made two mistakes and they punished us with their quality."

On cautions and a confrontation with a Newcastle member of staff after full-time:

"Normal football talk. What happens on the pitch, stays on the pitch. Emotions are very high, and when the other team has three or four techincal staff in the area, they should get yellows too.

"Both teams were trying to give instructions to the team - I think the referees can be more patient with the bench."
